Headquartered in New York with roughly 2,000 employees across offices in Los Angeles, Chattanooga, Chicago, Miami, Toronto, Amsterdam, London, Mexico City, Sydney, Mumbai, Tokyo, Kuala Lumpur, Singapore, and Bangkok, the agency serves clients including Bose, Coach, Diageo, Duracell, Indeed, Jimmy John's, Meta, Mondelez, NatWest, PepsiCo, Tinder, and Wingstop. VaynerMedia is the flagship brand of holding company VaynerX, whose portfolio also includes Gallery Media Group, ChukMedia, Tamara Group, Eva Nosidam Productions, VaynerSpeakers, Tingley Lane, and the Marketing for the Now podcast. VaynerMedia is a services agency, not an API or platform company — it does not publish a developer API, SDK, or public technology product, and its public GitHub presence (github.com/vaynermedia and github.com/vaynerx) consists primarily of forked open source libraries and internal build tooling rather than maintained API products.

companies.name: CRED
companies.description: CRED is an Indian consumer fintech that started with premium credit-card bill payments and rewards and has expanded into peer-to-peer payments (Scan & Pay, Tap to Pay, RuPay credit card on UPI), short-term credit (CRED Cash, CRED Mint), wealth (CRED Money), e-commerce (CRED Store), and travel. CRED's surface area is overwhelmingly consumer-app and the company does not publish a public, self-service developer portal. Its engineering organisation contributes to the broader ecosystem via the engineering.cred.club tech blog and open-source repositories under the CRED-CLUB GitHub org. B2B integrations (merchant acceptance, issuer partnerships, etc.) are negotiated directly with the partnerships team.

companies.name: Heyzap
companies.description: Heyzap was a mobile-game advertising, discovery, and monetization company. It began as a social game-discovery network and pivoted into a mobile ad mediation platform, offering iOS, Android, Unity, Cordova, and Adobe AIR/ANE SDKs that let game developers serve and mediate ads across networks such as AdMob, AppLovin, Vungle, Chartboost, AdColony, and Facebook Audience Network. Heyzap was acquired by Fyber (RNTS Media) in 2016 and its brand was later folded into Digital Turbine. Heyzap never published a public REST API; its developer surface was the mobile ad-mediation SDKs distributed via GitHub (github.com/Heyzap) and package registries. The heyzap.com domain is now parked/for-sale and the developer documentation site no longer resolves; this profile preserves the historical, first-party SDK artifacts that remain publicly available. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Union Square Ventures.

companies.name: Remarkable AI
companies.description: Remarkable AI is an AI-powered customer engagement platform for consumer and ecommerce brands, delivering 1:1 personalized messaging across email, SMS, and social channels. Its products span Retain (personalized win-back campaigns for lapsed customers), Support (24/7 AI-plus-human customer service that converts tickets into sales), and Acquire (AI-driven social engagement on TikTok, YouTube, X, and Reddit). The platform is used by 1,000+ ecommerce brands including SAXX, Hyper Skin, Nomadica, Kindra, StoryWorth, and Hot Topic, with plans starting at $1,500/month. Remarkable AI was surfaced as a portfolio company of Partech and added to the API Evangelist network. It publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation as of this enrichment pass.

companies.name: Bizible Marketing Analytics
companies.description: Bizible was a B2B marketing attribution and revenue analytics platform that connected marketing activity to pipeline and revenue across advertising, web, CRM, and marketing-automation channels. Acquired by Marketo in 2018 and subsequently by Adobe, the product now ships as Adobe Marketo Measure (formerly Bizible); the bizible.com domain 301-redirects to Adobe and its product documentation has moved to the Adobe Experience League. It has no standalone public developer portal, OpenAPI, or API reference of its own — integration is handled through Adobe/Marketo Measure and CRM connectors.

companies.name: Clarabridge
companies.description: Clarabridge was a customer experience management (CEM) and conversational analytics company known for its natural-language-understanding platform that analyzed unstructured customer feedback — contact-center transcripts, chat, email, surveys, social media, and online reviews — to surface sentiment, emotion, effort, intent, and emerging topics. Qualtrics acquired Clarabridge in 2021, and the technology has since been integrated and rebranded inside the Qualtrics XM platform: Clarabridge Studio became Qualtrics XM Discover and Clarabridge Engage became Qualtrics Connect. Clarabridge no longer operates an independent developer portal or public API; its capabilities are now delivered through Qualtrics. This profile is retained as a company/brand record in the API Evangelist network with an acquisition pointer to Qualtrics.

companies.name: CrawlGraph
companies.description: A backlink-intelligence SaaS built on Common Crawl's open hyperlink graph (~120M domains / 4.4B links). Provides referring-domain lookups, competitor gap analysis, and outreach-target discovery as a low-cost alternative to Ahrefs/Moz/Semrush.

companies.name: Doubleclick
companies.description: DoubleClick was a pioneering digital advertising technology company founded in 1995 and backed by Canaan Partners; it went public in 1998 and was acquired by Google in 2007-2008. Its products were absorbed into what is now the Google Marketing Platform: DoubleClick Campaign Manager became Campaign Manager 360, DoubleClick for Publishers (DFP) became Google Ad Manager, and DoubleClick Bid Manager became Display & Video 360. DoubleClick no longer operates as an independent company and maintains no independent developer portal, website, or API host of its own. The surviving developer/API lineage (dfareporting / doubleclick-advertisers) is served entirely through Google's developer platform. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead record; there is no independent provider surface to enrich.

companies.name: IKEA U.S.
companies.description: IKEA U.S. is the United States retail operation of IKEA, run by Ingka Group, the largest IKEA franchisee. The U.S. business operates ~50+ full-service stores, ~40+ Plan & Order Points, and ~80+ pick-up locations across the country, alongside the ikea.com/us e-commerce site and the IKEA mobile app. Inter IKEA Systems B.V. separately owns the IKEA Concept and brand. IKEA U.S. offers home furnishings, kitchens, appliances, lighting, the IKEA Family loyalty program, the IKEA Business Network for B2B customers, home delivery and Click & Collect, design and planning services, the Buy Back & Resell program, and IKEA Home smart products controlled via the IKEA Home smart and IKEA Home smart 1 apps. IKEA U.S. does not publish a public developer API; supplier and trading-partner integrations are handled through IKEA's vendor systems and Ingka Group's internal digital platforms.

companies.name: Interpublic Group
companies.description: The Interpublic Group of Companies (IPG) is one of the world's largest advertising and marketing services holding companies, with networks including McCann Worldgroup, IPG Mediabrands, FCB, MullenLowe Group, and Acxiom. In 2024 Omnicom announced its acquisition of IPG and operates combined brand operations under omc.com. IPG does not publish a unified public developer portal or open REST APIs; technology surfaces are delivered through agency-network products such as Acxiom data services and Mediabrands' identity and measurement platforms.

companies.name: OwnLocal
companies.description: OwnLocal is an Austin-based automated digital advertising platform for local media companies. It helps newspapers, local publishers, and media companies power their digital services by automatically converting traditional print advertisements into online marketing campaigns, extending advertiser reach across search, social, and display channels. OwnLocal was a 500 Global portfolio company; its current public surface is a marketing site with no published developer or API program.

companies.name: Persado
companies.description: Persado is an enterprise AI platform that generates and optimizes marketing and customer-communication language, built for regulated industries such as financial services, insurance, healthcare, and retail. Its Motivation AI models produce compliant, on-brand message variants, score them for predicted performance, and personalize every send automatically, integrating with marketing platforms including Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Adobe Campaign, and Braze. Persado is delivered through enterprise contracts and platform integrations; it does not currently publish a public self-service developer API, developer portal, or SDKs. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of bain-capital-ventures and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

companies.name: Prose
companies.description: Prose is a New York City-based direct-to-consumer beauty company that makes truly custom haircare and skincare. Customers complete an online consultation covering hair type, scalp, lifestyle, diet, and local environment, and Prose then formulates personalized shampoo, conditioner, hair masks, supplements, and skincare made to order and sold primarily through a subscription model. Prose was surfaced as a portfolio company of forerunner-ventures and insight-partners. It operates no public developer API; its verified GitHub organization publishes internal tooling and third-party client libraries only, so this profile carries company identity and a domain-security probe rather than API artifacts.

companies.name: Altitude Software
companies.description: Altitude Software is a contact center and unified customer interaction (uCI) software company founded in 1993 and headquartered in Lisbon, Portugal. Its flagship Altitude uCI suite provides omnichannel contact center capabilities — inbound/outbound campaigns, IVR and self-service, routing, dialer, recording and quality management, and CRM/ERP integration — with the Altitude uAgent SDK exposing Java, C/C++, .NET, SOAP, XML-RPC and web-service APIs for on-premises and cloud deployments. Altitude Software was a portfolio company of Insight Partners and was acquired by Enghouse Systems (TSX: ENGH) on 2020-12-30; the product line is now developed and maintained by Enghouse Interactive, and the brand continues to operate regionally (e.g. Altitude Software APAC). The company does not publish a modern public REST API, developer portal, or OpenAPI specification; integration is delivered through the proprietary uAgent SDK and packaged CRM/ERP connectors.

companies.name: InsightEra
companies.description: InsightEra Co., Ltd. is a Bangkok-based marketing technology and data intelligence company that builds ready-to-use online marketing tools from social network data. Its platform spans social research (social listening and competitor analytics), social management (omni-channel management and chatbots), social data and analytics (Customer Data Platform and CRM), and social campaigns (campaign targeting and analytics), alongside a Thai NLP service and a generative enterprise AI platform. InsightEra positions its "Intelligence Model" as an ecosystem that connects external intelligence (market, customers, competitors, society) with internal organizational data so brands can turn insight into interaction and action. The company was surfaced as a portfolio lead of lightspeed-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network. No public developer API, documentation, or specification surface was found during enrichment; this profile captures the company's public identity only.

companies.name: LemonBox
companies.description: LemonBox (来檬) is a health-technology brand working in AI-generative personalized nutrition. Founded in 2016 in Silicon Valley, incubated at the University of Chicago Polsky Center in 2017, and accepted into Y Combinator in 2018, it entered the Chinese market that year and is now headquartered in Shanghai. LemonBox builds individualized daily vitamin and supplement packs from a three-minute FFQ (food frequency questionnaire) nutrition assessment scored by its LemonAlgo adaptive engine, then fulfills them one pack at a time (MOQ=1) through its Personalization Fulfillment Center in Hong Kong. The company reports serving more than 10 million cumulative users as of 2026 and sells both direct-to-consumer and B2B. Investors include Y Combinator and Partech. LemonBox operates a consumer web and WeChat mini-program experience and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; its agent-facing surface is limited to a published /llms.txt and a robots.txt that explicitly allow-lists generative-AI crawlers.

companies.name: Lumific
companies.description: Lumific is a client reactivation platform for med spas that reconnects dormant clients with a practice to recover revenue from high-value treatments. Its proprietary system identifies inactive clients in an existing CRM (such as Mindbody or Zenoti) and launches automated, multi-channel outreach campaigns combining personalized text messaging, professional phone calls, and instant gift-card offers to drive bookings. Campaigns launch within 24 hours, pricing is performance-based (commission only on completed treatments), and the service is TCPA and HIPAA compliant with market exclusivity limited to a few clinics per area. Lumific was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. This provider currently publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface.

companies.name: Markerly
companies.description: Markerly is a full-service influencer marketing agency, running creator campaigns since 2012 across strategy, vetted-creator sourcing, content, activation, and real-time measurement. Two specialties set the Austin, Texas agency apart: influencer campaigns for government agencies, public health, and nonprofits (advocacy), and bilingual/multicultural creator campaigns. Markerly operates managed campaigns and a creator network rather than a public developer API; it was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and profiled in the API Evangelist network. This enrichment pass confirmed a marketing/agency surface (site, llms.txt, robots.txt) with no public API, OpenAPI, MCP, or developer portal.

companies.name: Filmgrail
companies.description: Filmgrail is an Oslo, Norway based software company offering an AI-powered digital platform for cinema operators. Its product suite bundles a cinema content management system (CMS), native iOS and Android mobile apps, branded cinema websites, and marketing and analytics tooling into a single managed offering, with a loyalty system, festival platform, push notifications, and a planning tool layered on top. Filmgrail markets these capabilities as a way to automate cinema operations and grow digital ticket sales and moviegoer engagement, and describes API-based integration between its platform and cinema point-of-sale systems, websites, and mobile apps. Backed by 500 Global, the company operates from Oslo, Norway and Delaware, USA. Filmgrail does not currently publish a public developer portal, API reference, or client SDKs; this profile is maintained as an API Evangelist network company record.

companies.name: Headgum
companies.description: Headgum is an American comedy podcast network founded in 2015 by Marty Michael, Amir Blumenfeld, and Jake Hurwitz, with studios in Los Angeles and New York. It produces and distributes premium comedy and entertainment podcasts including Doughboys, Not Another D&D Podcast, Dead Eyes, Hey Riddle Riddle, and Why Won't You Date Me?, and operates Gumball, a host-read podcast and YouTube advertising marketplace that lets brands buy ads directly from creators. Headgum is a portfolio company of Union Square Ventures. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; as of this pass Headgum publishes no public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI surface.

companies.name: Motif Analytics
companies.description: Motif Analytics was a startup (founded 2021 by Mikhail Panko and Theron Ji, with Sean Taylor as chief scientist) building interactive sequence analytics for growth and operations teams. Its product let analysts explore event sequences — user journeys, funnels, order-management flows — with a purpose-built Sequence Operations Language (SOL) and in-browser WebAssembly so data never had to leave the browser, backed by a $5.7M seed round led by Amplify Partners and Felicis (2024). As of this enrichment pass the product site and the docs.motifanalytics.com subdomain no longer resolve and motifanalytics.com serves a MarkMonitor brand-protection holding page, indicating the company has wound down. No public REST/GraphQL API, SDK, OpenAPI, CLI, or developer surface was ever published; the sole public GitHub repo is a 2023 bug reproduction.

companies.name: Realtor.com
companies.description: Realtor.com is a real estate listings website operated by Move, Inc., a subsidiary of News Corp, headquartered in Santa Clara, California. The platform is the official site of the National Association of REALTORS (NAR) under a long-term operating agreement and is one of the largest U.S. property search portals, serving home buyers, sellers, renters, and real estate professionals. Realtor.com aggregates for-sale, for-rent, and off-market listings sourced primarily from Multiple Listing Services (MLSs) via Move's listings distribution subsidiary ListHub, and surfaces them through consumer web and mobile apps alongside neighborhood, school, mortgage, and market data. The professional side of the business sells lead-generation and marketing products such as Connections Plus, ReadyConnect Concierge, and Market VIP to agents and brokers, while ListHub provides MLS-to-portal syndication, broker reporting, and listing feed management. Adjacent Move properties include Doorsteps, Moving.com, and SeniorHousingNet, and the company publishes a public economic research arm at realtor.com/research that releases monthly housing market reports and downloadable historical datasets. Realtor.com does not publish a first-party public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK; programmatic access to listing data is gated through MLS membership and ListHub's broker/vendor agreements, while the only widely available HTTP APIs branded as Realtor.com are unofficial third-party scrapers hosted on RapidAPI and Apify.

companies.name: Triblio
companies.description: Triblio is an account-based marketing (ABM) platform now owned by Foundry, the marketing services and data unit of International Data Group (IDG). Originally founded in Reston, Virginia, Triblio was acquired by IDG/Foundry in June 2020 as the cornerstone of a multi-year strategy to combine first- party publisher data, third-party intent signals, and ABM advertising, web personalization, and sales acceleration into a single platform. The product combines account-based advertising, intent-driven audience segmentation, website personalization, and a Smart Score that ranks accounts using behavioral signals from first-party web visits, third-party intent providers (notably Bombora Company Surge and G2 intent), CRM data, and Foundry's own publisher network. Triblio integrates with major CRMs and marketing automation systems including Salesforce, HubSpot, Microsoft Dynamics 365, SugarCRM, Marketo, Pardot, LinkedIn Campaign Manager, Google Analytics, and Slack. Foundry positions Triblio as the engine behind its broader Sales Acceleration and Foundry ABM offerings, with intent data feeds from Bombora ingested weekly and G2 intent ingested nightly. Triblio does not publish a public developer API portal, OpenAPI specification, or open-source SDKs; the GitHub organization at github.com/triblio was archived in January 2026 with no public repos. Customer integrations are delivered through pre-built CRM and MAP connectors, an Apps Marketplace, and platform-internal automation rather than a self-serve developer API.

companies.name: Banksight
companies.description: BankSight Systems is a cloud banking software company founded in 2015 (San Francisco / Mumbai) that built an intelligent banking CRM and customer engagement platform for community banks, regional banks, and credit unions. The platform consolidated and analyzed customer data on top of Microsoft Azure and the Microsoft Power Platform, running a banking-specific data model with an open integration framework of pre-built connectors to core, LOS, and legacy banking systems, and delivered AI-driven "Next Best Conversation" recommendations to bankers and wealth managers. BankSight was acquired by Bottomline Technologies; its product now lives inside Bottomline's Commercial Digital Banking platform, and banksight.com 301-redirects to bottomline.com. This profile was surfaced as a Bloomberg Beta portfolio company (since exited) and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

companies.name: Fivestars
companies.description: Fivestars was a customer loyalty, rewards, and payments platform for small and mid-sized brick-and-mortar merchants, founded in 2010 and headquartered in San Francisco. It combined an automated marketing engine, a customer loyalty and rewards program, and integrated card payments so local businesses could turn one-time shoppers into repeat customers. Fivestars was backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, Menlo Ventures, and Y Combinator, and historically operated a developer program exposing loyalty, promotions, and customer APIs. The company was acquired by SumUp in 2021 and its product has since been folded into SumUp Connect (SumUp Loyalty); the fivestars.com domain now redirects to SumUp's loyalty program and the standalone Fivestars developer portal and public APIs have been retired. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical company record.

companies.name: Healthy Labs
companies.description: Healthy Labs is a healthcare and insurance technology company that powers a portfolio of digital health brands driving membership growth for Medicare and ACA (Affordable Care Act) insurance providers. Its offerings center on consumer lead generation, compliance and operational analytics, and member acquisition and retention optimization for the health-insurance market. The company has since rebranded as MPA (mpa.com), positioning itself as an AI-powered platform for licensed insurance professionals and agencies. Surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub, this profile is enriched from public sources; no public developer program, OpenAPI specification, or API surface was found at the time of enrichment.

companies.name: LevelUp
companies.description: LevelUp (thelevelup.com) was a mobile payments and loyalty platform that let consumers pay and earn rewards at local restaurants and businesses via a QR-code / mobile-order-ahead app, and gave merchants a way to increase engagement and loyalty. It launched in March 2011 as a spinoff of SCVNGR and historically ran a developer API for payments, ordering, and loyalty at developer.thelevelup.com. LevelUp was acquired by Grubhub in 2018 for $390 million; as of this enrichment pass the entire thelevelup.com domain 302-redirects to grubhub.com and the former developer.thelevelup.com and api.thelevelup.com subdomains no longer resolve, so there is no independent live API surface remaining to catalog. This profile is retained as a historical network record of an acquired company.

companies.name: TrialPay
companies.description: TrialPay was an alternative-payments and offer-based advertising company founded in 2006 and based in Mountain View, California, backed by Battery Ventures among others. Its platform let merchants and game developers offer users a product for "free" in exchange for completing an advertiser-sponsored action (a purchase, trial, or signup), with the advertiser paying the merchant — monetizing users who would not otherwise pay. TrialPay shipped web, Android, and iOS SDKs plus offer-wall and monetization APIs (e.g. GetBuyCoinsInfo / GetBuyDirectInfo) widely used in social and mobile games. Visa acquired TrialPay in April 2015 and folded the technology into the Visa Commerce Network; TrialPay no longer operates as a standalone company and its public developer surface (help.trialpay.com, trialpay.com) is offline.

companies.name: App-CM
companies.description: App-CM, Inc. (株式会社アップシーエム) is a Tokyo-based technology company that operates a proprietary video-advertising delivery platform for smartphones, using in-house compression, delivery, and targeting-algorithm technology to serve video ads smoothly in mobile environments. App-CM also develops and publishes consumer mobile apps including FriendQuiz, SunQ, and Shakin. The company is backed by 500 Global and is profiled in the API Evangelist network. It publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specifications at this time; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture.

companies.name: Empirix
companies.description: Empirix was a communications and contact-center test, assurance, and monitoring company backed by Matrix Partners. Its products spanned network and application performance testing, VoIP and IVR quality assurance, contact-center monitoring, and end-to-end customer-experience assurance for carriers and enterprises. Empirix was acquired by Infovista in 2020; its testing and monitoring portfolio now operates under the Hammer Technologies brand, which is evolving into VistaCX (Voice Explorer, CallMaster, VoiceWatch, HammerRTC, VistaOne). The company exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI definition, or developer portal; empirix.com now redirects to hammer.com. This profile is a network stub enriched from public web surfaces only.

companies.name: Famebit
companies.description: Famebit was an influencer-marketing marketplace, founded in 2013 and headquartered in Los Angeles, that connected YouTube, Instagram, and Vine creators with brands for sponsored branded-content campaigns. Backed by 500 Startups (500 Global), it was acquired by Google in October 2016, rebranded as "FameBit by YouTube," and later folded into YouTube BrandConnect. The standalone platform has been shut down and famebit.com now redirects to a Google/YouTube Help support page, so there is no live public API, developer portal, or documentation to enrich.

companies.name: Yieldify *
companies.description: Yieldify is a website personalization and conversion rate optimization (CRO) platform for ecommerce brands, founded in 2013 in London by Jay Radia and backed by investors including GV (Google Ventures). Its SaaS platform delivers targeted on-site messaging, customer-journey personalization, and A/B testing to lift conversion and revenue. Yieldify was acquired by Publicis Groupe in January 2023 and folded into Epsilon, where it is now offered as the "Accelerate" (Yieldify) platform; yieldify.com now redirects to Epsilon. The product is delivered as a hosted, managed marketing service with a customer help center rather than a public developer API — no public REST/OpenAPI surface, SDK, or developer portal was found during enrichment.

companies.name: ARI
companies.description: ARI (shopARI) is a New York City based artificial intelligence company building a personal shopping and styling assistant for fashion. The product is positioned as an AI stylist that produces custom style recommendations across a curated marketplace of both major and independent brands, interpreting the intent and sentiment behind a shopper request rather than matching product tags alone. The company was founded by Lior Cole and has raised pre-seed capital from investors including Bloomberg Beta, 1517 Fund, Correlation Ventures, Daybreak Ventures and Z Fellows. As of this enrichment pass ARI operates as a consumer application and publishes no public developer API, documentation portal, SDKs or machine-readable specification; the shopari.com domain is registered and carries mail records but resolves no web address record.

companies.name: BBDO Worldwide
companies.description: BBDO Worldwide is a global advertising agency network founded in 1928 and headquartered in New York City. It is the largest of the creative-agency networks owned by Omnicom Group, with roughly 15,000 employees across approximately 289 offices in 81 countries (per Wikipedia, citing company data). The agency's positioning is "Do Big Things," and its public work is campaign-led — Pepsi, Budweiser, McDonald's, M&M's, Snickers, Visa, AT&T Business, Volkswagen, Skoda, Whiskas, and many more. BBDO has been named Cannes Lions Network of the Year multiple times since 2007 and Network of the Decade in 2020. BBDO does not publish a developer portal, public REST APIs, OpenAPI specifications, SDKs, status page, or pricing — its product is creative work delivered to brand clients, not software offered to developers. This repository indexes the public properties (homepage, network site, news, parent company, GitHub org, and notable agency network members) so the API Evangelist network can track the absence of a developer surface and link BBDO to its parent Omnicom and sibling networks (DDB Worldwide, TBWA Worldwide).

companies.name: Bidgely
companies.description: Bidgely is a Mountain View, California energy analytics company that builds AI software for electric and gas utilities. Its flagship platform, UtilityAI, applies patented non-intrusive load monitoring (NILM) and disaggregation techniques to smart meter interval data to infer appliance-level energy usage — air conditioning, heat pumps, electric vehicles, pool pumps, water heaters and more — from the whole-home meter signal alone, without surveys, sub-meters, or smart plugs. The platform layers GenAI natural-language interfaces and Agentic AI workflows on top of disaggregation to support utility programs across demand-side management, customer engagement and high-bill alerts, load flexibility and time-of-use, electrification (EV and heat pump targeting), grid resiliency and DER planning, affordability and income-qualified outreach, gas efficiency, small and mid-sized business programs, and energy theft detection. Bidgely is sold to utilities as SaaS or deployable into customer AWS, Snowflake, Databricks, Azure, and Oracle environments, and exposes embeddable customer-facing widgets to utility digital channels. Bidgely has been deployed by more than 50 utilities across four continents — including FortisBC, Arizona Public Service, PacifiCorp, Avista, NV Energy, Nova Scotia Power, and SoCalGas — covering tens of millions of meters. Bidgely operates an internal REST API surface across regional endpoints (naapi.bidgely.com, api.eu.bidgely.com) for its own pilot deployments and embeddable widgets, but does not currently publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or self-service API key program; integration is conducted under utility contracts.

companies.name: ClippPR
companies.description: ClippPR (later rebranded Primeloop) was a startup that helped brands and PR agencies clip and track their press coverage, measure the value of earned media, and re-engage audiences by turning clicks on shared links into targeted relationships. Founded around 2011 in Las Vegas and part of 500 Startups' eighth (first San Francisco) accelerator batch, the company has since shut down. Its primeloop.com domain is parked/for-sale, primeloop.co no longer resolves, and clipppr.com has been taken over by an unrelated blog. No public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI was ever published; the only surviving first-party surface is the company's GitHub organization.

companies.name: Databolt
companies.description: Databolt is a digital design agency that builds software applications, websites, and custom web platforms for startups and businesses. The agency offers UI/UX design, web development, WordPress and Prestashop premium themes, SEO services, and operates GPU- and CPU-optimized clusters for rendering and computational data processing.

companies.name: Datanyze *
companies.description: Datanyze is a sales intelligence and technographic data provider owned by ZoomInfo. It offers a free browser (Chrome) extension that surfaces business contact information — work email addresses, direct-dial and mobile phone numbers, and company firmographics — for prospects on LinkedIn profiles and company websites. Datanyze pioneered "technographics," the practice of tracking the web technologies and software a company uses to power targeted B2B sales and marketing outreach. ZoomInfo acquired Datanyze in 2018 to deliver real-time technographic data to its customers. No public developer API is currently documented; this profile captures the company's discoverable web and security surface.

companies.name: Echo AI (fka Pathlight)
companies.description: Echo AI (formerly Pathlight) was an AI-driven customer conversation intelligence platform used by customer-experience and support teams to analyze support conversations, surface hidden insights, and coach agents. It was a portfolio company of Insight Partners. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no discoverable public developer surface — no API documentation, OpenAPI, SDKs, or MCP server — and its marketing domains are offline (pathlight.com no longer resolves and echoai.com returns a removed Framer site). The only verified live public asset is the company's GitHub organization, whose public repositories are forks of third-party libraries and Singer.io data-ingestion taps used internally rather than any first-party client library. This profile is retained as an identity record; no fabricated API artifacts were added.

companies.name: Gigacatalyst
companies.description: Gigacatalyst is a Y Combinator-backed enterprise AI platform that turns customer requirements into configured software demos, POCs, UAT environments, and implementation workspaces by writing real configurations through a customer's existing product APIs. It embeds an AI customization layer directly into SaaS applications so that sales, solutions-engineering, and customer-success teams can build the missing features and workflows they need using natural language, while inheriting the host product's authentication and role-based access controls, sandboxed execution, and AI model restrictions. Gigacatalyst is an API consumer: it operates on top of other providers' APIs rather than publishing its own public developer API, so this profile captures company identity and public web properties rather than API artifacts.

companies.name: Klout
companies.description: Klout was a San Francisco social-analytics company, founded in 2008 by Joe Fernandez and Binh Tran, that scored individuals on their online social influence. The "Klout Score" was a single number from 1 to 100 derived from the size of a person's social network and how other people engaged with the content they published across connected accounts such as Twitter, Facebook, LinkedIn, Instagram, and Google+. Klout operated a public REST API — the Klout API v2 at api.klout.com — that let developers resolve a social handle to a Klout identity, look up a user's score and score history, and retrieve influence graphs (who a user influences and is influenced by) and topic affinities; access was key-based and widely used by marketing, CRM, and social-listening tools, and a large community of third-party client libraries grew up around it in Ruby, Node.js, Python, and PHP. Lithium Technologies acquired Klout on 27 March 2014 for approximately $200 million. Lithium retired Klout as a standalone service on 25 May 2018 — the day the EU General Data Protection Regulation took effect — stating that Klout's AI and machine-learning capabilities were valuable to Lithium but the consumer service was not aligned with its long-term strategy. The Klout API was shut down with the service. Lithium has since been rebranded as Khoros, and klout.com now redirects into the Khoros website. The company is defunct and operates no live API; this profile is retained as a historical provider record in the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: MoPub
companies.description: MoPub was a mobile advertising and app-monetization platform providing ad-network mediation, advanced bidding, and a real-time marketplace/exchange plus open-source iOS and Android SDKs for mobile publishers. Founded in 2010, it was acquired by Twitter in 2013, then sold to AppLovin for $1.05B in a deal that closed January 2022. AppLovin migrated publishers to its MAX platform and shut down MoPub's mediation, advanced bidding, and marketplace on 2022-03-31, with dashboard/reporting retired by 2022-04-30. MoPub is now defunct: www.mopub.com redirects to applovin.com and the developer/API surface (developers.mopub.com) is offline. This profile is retained as a historical/defunct record; there is no live MoPub API to enrich.

companies.name: MorphL
companies.description: MorphL was an AI and machine learning platform for e-commerce and digital publishing personalization, offering a suite of API-based, fully-automated models that predicted user behaviors (shopping stage, churn, search intent) to power click-through, conversion, and personalization KPIs across the customer journey. Founded circa 2017 and funded through the Google Digital News Initiative, the European Data Incubator, and the Techstars Montreal AI accelerator, MorphL also shipped an open-source MorphL Community Edition (big-data + Spark/Cassandra ML pipeline). MorphL was acquired by Algolia in January 2021 to power Algolia's AI-driven predictive experiences and personalization. The company's product APIs and hosted developer surface are no longer operated as a standalone service; the morphl.ai and morphl.io domains no longer resolve. The archived open-source code remains public under the Morphl-AI GitHub organization.

companies.name: Placester
companies.description: Placester is a real estate marketing and technology platform that provides IDX-enabled websites, CRM, lead generation, and marketing automation tools for real estate agents, teams, and brokerages. Historically Placester published a developer-facing Real Estate API (api.placester.com) for listings, contacts, and website content, but the developer portal (developer.placester.com) now redirects to a site-unavailable page, indicating the public developer program is discontinued or inaccessible. This profile was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; no accessible public API surface, OpenAPI, or SDK was found at enrichment time.

companies.name: Revv
companies.description: Revv (formerly RevvSales) is a document automation and electronic-signature platform that helps businesses prepare, automate, and execute business paperwork such as sales contracts, proposals, and agreements. The product offers 1,000+ customizable document templates, drag-and-drop editing, rule-based approval workflows, eSignatures with audit trails, real-time collaboration, and analytics, plus integrations with Salesforce, HubSpot, Google Sheets, and Zapier alongside a native REST API. Founded in India and backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, Revv was acquired by LegalZoom; its standalone developer and API-documentation subdomains (apidocs.revv.so, docs.revv.so, help.revv.so) now redirect into the LegalZoom application, so no independently documented Revv API specification is currently published.

companies.name: Simplifai Labs
companies.description: Simplifai Labs is a Dubai-based artificial intelligence and marketing-technology company founded in 2018 by Sachin Rathnaraj Jain. Its deep-learning platform combines image recognition, computer vision, sentiment and emotion analysis, and natural language processing to place brand advertising alongside highly relevant, brand-safe content in real time, without relying on stored user cookie data. Simplifai Labs completed the 500 Global (Misk 500 MENA) accelerator in Riyadh and is a 500 Global portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer documentation, or SDKs, and its original simplifailabs.com domain now resolves to an unrelated hosting provider, so no API artifacts could be harvested.

companies.name: ThriveHive
companies.description: ThriveHive was a Boston-based guided marketing platform for small businesses (10 or fewer employees), founded in 2011 by Max Faingezicht and Adam Blake and part of the Techstars Boston 2015 class. It was acquired by Propel Marketing (GateHouse Media) in 2016 for $11.8M and the brand was folded into Gannett's LocaliQ after the 2019 GateHouse-Gannett merger. The company published no public API or developer portal; thrivehive.com now serves LocaliQ content behind an expired TLS certificate.

companies.name: Wawa
companies.description: Wawa is a privately held, family-owned convenience store and fuel retail chain headquartered in Pennsylvania. Founded in 1803 as a dairy farm and operating convenience stores since 1964, Wawa runs approximately 1,100 stores across Pennsylvania, New Jersey, Delaware, Maryland, Virginia, Florida, North Carolina, Indiana, and Alabama. The company is a regional fresh-food, beverage, and fuel brand with a strong loyalty program (Wawa Rewards) and a mobile ordering app. Wawa operates an internal API management platform (built with MuleSoft) used to connect to third-party services such as Uber Eats, Grubhub, and DoorDash for delivery, but does not publish a public developer portal or expose public APIs.

companies.name: Workbounce
companies.description: Workbounce was an AI-powered revenue and sales enablement platform that gave sales reps instant answers to deal-blocking questions by connecting company documents and knowledge to AI-powered search, delivered through a Slack bot and Chrome extension. Co-founded by Adam Smith and Rowan Bailey and backed by Index Ventures. As of July 2026 workbounce.com returns HTTP 402 (Vercel DEPLOYMENT_DISABLED) and the company appears defunct; no public API, developer docs, SDKs, or packages were ever published.

companies.name: Wupima
companies.description: Wupima, Inc. was a Virginia-based mobile social intelligence company that did business as Hook Mobile, backed by 500 Global (500 Startups). Its App Growth Engine (AGE) product offered iOS and Android SDKs and an API that let mobile app and game developers grow their user base through word-of-mouth SMS/MMS social invitations, device targeting, and conversion analytics. The company, founded by Terry Hsiao, was active roughly 2010-2016 and is now defunct - wupima.com is a dead S3 bucket (403 AllAccessDisabled) and hookmobile.com has been taken over by an unrelated domain squatter serving spam, so no live website, developer portal, or API surface remains. Profile retained as a historical 500 Global portfolio record.

companies.name: Assist
companies.description: Assist (assi.st) was a San Francisco conversational-commerce platform founded in 2015 by Shane Mac, Giovanni Vatieri, and Geek Squad founder Robert Stephens, and backed by Slow Ventures. Assist built branded chatbot and voice assistant experiences that let consumers order, book, and pay inside messaging channels, running deployments for brands including Fandango, 1-800-Flowers, and Hyatt across Facebook Messenger, Telegram, Twitter, Apple Business Chat, Amazon Alexa, and Google Assistant, where it shipped one of the first Google Actions at launch in 2016. Conversocial acquired Assist in March 2019 and Shane Mac became Conversocial's Chief Automation Officer. The assi.st domain is now parked with no web host, and Assist never published a public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API specification, so there is no API surface to catalog.

companies.name: Cerenovus
companies.description: Cerenovus (cerenovus.ai) is a San Francisco AI software company backed by Y Combinator (Summer 2026 batch), founded in 2026 by a team out of Harvard and NYU Stern. It builds "the AI company brain" — software that reads everything a company produces (email, chat, documents, CRM, ERP, tickets, meeting notes) and returns findings with citations back to the source. Its products are Noesis (the enterprise flagship company brain built for CEOs, CFOs, and private-equity operating partners), Midas (an AI sales platform that runs inside a company's existing CRM and is paid out of the revenue it produces), and Compendium (shared real-time context and durable memory for engineering and customer-facing teams and their AI agents, including shared Claude Code sessions). Cerenovus is not affiliated with the similarly named Johnson & Johnson MedTech neurovascular device business.

companies.name: GazeHawk
companies.description: GazeHawk was a webcam-based eye-tracking startup founded in December 2009 by Brian Krausz and Joe Gershenson, offering affordable eye-tracking usability and ad-testing services that ran on ordinary consumer webcams instead of expensive dedicated hardware. Backed by Y Combinator (S10) and 500 Startups, the company was acqui-hired by Facebook in March 2012 — Facebook hired the engineering team but explicitly did not acquire the product or technology, and the founders moved on to unrelated backend and product engineering. GazeHawk operated no public API, developer portal, or SDKs; the domain today serves only a legacy static marketing and blog site for the defunct product.

companies.name: GrowthHackers
companies.description: A private community for top growth leaders - where marketing, product, and growth experts come to learn, connect, and tackle challenges together.

companies.name: Minute Media
companies.description: Minute Media is a global technology, media, and advertising company that builds and operates digital sports and entertainment content brands while licensing publishing and monetization technology to third parties. Its owned-and-operated properties include Sports Illustrated, The Players' Tribune, 90min, Mental Floss, FanSided, The Big Lead, and DBLTAP, reaching a reported 200+ million monthly users. On the technology side it offers the STN Online Video Platform (OVP) for video publishing and monetization, a Minute Media SSP for programmatic advertising, and ad-management solutions for publishers. Minute Media was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this pass the company publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API definitions on its primary web properties.

companies.name: Ogilvy
companies.description: Ogilvy is a global advertising, marketing, and communications agency network founded by David Ogilvy in 1948 and headquartered in New York City. It is a WPP company (NASDAQ: WPPGY) operating across roughly 132 offices in 83 countries (per ogilvy.com/about; WPP cites 128 offices in 88 countries) with approximately 17,500 employees (per Wikipedia, as of 2022). The network positions itself around "Borderless Creativity," innovating at the intersections of five core capabilities: Advertising, Public Relations & Influence, Consulting, Relationship Design (OgilvyOne), and Health. Ogilvy was named Cannes Lions Network of the Year in 2022 and 2024, D&AD Network of the Year in 2020, and took Network of the Year at The One Show 2026. Long-standing client work includes Coca-Cola, Dove (Campaign for Real Beauty), IBM, American Express, IKEA, Hellmann's, Unilever, KFC, and Cadbury. Ogilvy does not publish a developer portal, public REST APIs, OpenAPI specifications, SDKs, status page, changelog, or pricing — its product is creative work delivered to brand clients, not software offered to developers. There is no `github.com/Ogilvy` organization. This repository indexes the public properties (homepage, capabilities, work, ideas/blog, parent company, regional sites, and notable sub-brands) so the API Evangelist network can track the absence of a developer surface and link Ogilvy to its parent WPP and to its practice-area brands (Ogilvy Health, OgilvyOne, Ogilvy PR, Ogilvy Consulting).

companies.name: SureWaves
companies.description: SureWaves is a broadcast-television advertising technology company that integrates linear TV with digital advertising infrastructure. It provides AI-powered spot and yield management for broadcasters and real-time, pay-for-performance campaign tooling for advertisers, and operates India's largest spot TV network — more than 20 million spots monthly across 550+ local channels reaching 490+ million households. Holder of 50+ patents, backed by Accel, with offices in Bangalore, New York, McLean, Mumbai and New Delhi. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub; enrichment found no public API, developer portal, or SDK surface as of 2026-07.

companies.name: TapAd
companies.description: Tapad is a digital identity and cross-device graph technology company, founded in 2010 and headquartered in New York City. Its flagship product, the Tapad Graph, is a probabilistic device graph that lets marketers, agencies, and platforms recognize a brand's customer or related household across the many devices they use, powering programmatic targeting, media measurement, attribution, and personalization. Tapad was acquired by the Norwegian telecom Telenor in 2016 and then by the credit-and-data company Experian in 2020, where its cross-device graph is offered as part of Experian's marketing and identity resolution portfolio. Tapad's technology is delivered primarily as a data partnership and graph-integration offering rather than a self-service public developer API; the company does not publish an open developer portal, API reference, or SDKs. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures.

companies.name: 24/7 Real Media
companies.description: 24/7 Real Media was a New York digital advertising technology and media company formed when 24/7 Media merged with Real Media in 2001, acquiring the Open AdStream publisher ad server. Venture-backed (Trinity Ventures, Zero Stage Capital) before its NASDAQ listing, it was acquired by WPP Group in July 2007 for approximately $649 million ($11.75 per share) and run inside WPP Digital. The business was renamed 24/7 Media, then merged into WPP's programmatic arm Xaxis in January 2014, retiring the 24/7 brand; Open AdStream was rebranded Xaxis for Publishers and sold to AppNexus later that year. Xaxis itself was sunset into GroupM Nexus in January 2024. The company is defunct: it operates no website, developer portal, or public API surface today.

companies.name: 60dB
companies.description: 60dB was a personalized short-form audio and podcast application built by Tiny Garage Labs, founded in 2016 by John Ciancutti, Steve Henn, and Steve McLendon. The app curated and recommended short radio-style audio stories tailored to a listener's habits, and was available on iOS, Android, and the web as well as through Alexa, Android Auto, and CarPlay. It was backed by Bloomberg Beta, Khosla Ventures, and Rivet Ventures. Google acqui-hired the founding team in October 2017 and the 60dB service was shut down on November 10, 2017. The company is defunct and publishes no developer program, API, or machine-readable interface today; the 60db.com domain now resolves to a parked placeholder page. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-company record for the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: AA Audience
companies.description: AA Audience is an adtech and data company that estimates a mobile user's credit score from their online activity using proprietary machine learning models. It collects data from partner mobile apps and ad networks, analyzes it, and connects with popular DSPs and DMPs so its clients - banks, credit card companies, and financial services firms - can target audiences interested in credit cards, loans, and financial services with guaranteed ROI. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. No public API, developer portal, or documentation surface was found during enrichment (the site is a single static marketing page).

companies.name: Absurd
companies.description: Absurd is an AI video creation platform positioning itself as "the Creative OS for AI video." It uses autonomous AI agents to handle scripting, scene planning, and video generation, letting companies produce brand and performance advertisements at scale in roughly 72 hours instead of weeks. Based in Los Angeles and part of Y Combinator's Fall 2025 batch, Absurd works with brands such as Hims, Kalshi, Replit, and Brex, with some of its generated videos reaching over a million organic views. As of this profile the company markets a product surface only (portfolio, careers, and contact pages) and does not publish a public API, developer documentation, or SDKs; this entry was enriched from public web sources and will be upgraded if a developer surface appears.

companies.name: Accompany
companies.description: Accompany was a relationship-intelligence startup that built people-and-company intelligence for executives, backed by Cowboy Ventures and CRV. It was acquired by Cisco (announced May 2018) and folded into Cisco's collaboration products; www.accompany.com is now a static acquisition-announcement page. Enrichment pass 2026-07-17 verified there is no live product, developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI, or any /.well-known/ or /llms.txt surface (the host is an nginx catch-all returning the same parked HTML for every path). No API artifacts exist to harvest; retained as a defunct/acquired VC-portfolio lead.

companies.name: Adap.tv
companies.description: Adap.tv was a global programmatic video advertising platform founded around 2007 and backed by Redpoint Ventures, offering brands, agencies, and publishers tools for planning, executing, and measuring video ad campaigns programmatically, including real-time bidding (RTB), audience targeting, campaign management, and analytics through its Pathway video-intelligence platform. AOL acquired Adap.tv in September 2013 for approximately $405 million and folded its technology into ONE by AOL; the business subsequently passed to Verizon Media and then Yahoo. Adap.tv no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no developer program, public API, or SDKs; the www.adap.tv domain now 301-redirects to yahooinc.com. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead record.

companies.name: Adelphic Mobile *
companies.description: Adelphic is an enterprise demand-side platform (DSP) for programmatic advertising, originally founded as a mobile-first programmatic buying platform and acquired by Viant Technology in 2017. The Adelphic DSP lets marketers plan, buy, and measure omnichannel campaigns across Connected TV, linear TV, mobile, desktop, streaming audio, and digital out-of-home from a single self-service interface, using Viant's people-based Household ID identity resolution to activate first- and third-party data and measure outcomes. It is offered as an enterprise SaaS platform with a hosted UI, online knowledge base, and certification/Programmatic University training rather than a public developer API; the adelphic.com domain now operates as a legacy redirect surface pointing to Viant's product pages. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company profile surfaced from GV.

companies.name: AdKnowledge
companies.description: Adknowledge, Inc. was a performance-based digital advertising and marketing technology holding company founded in 2004 by Scott Lynn and headquartered in Kansas City, Missouri. It ran a response-based targeting marketplace that connected advertisers to consumers across email, search, domains, social and app inventory, and it exposed a publisher-facing AdStation platform with an automated offer engine and creative library. Ben Legg served as Group CEO from 2011 to 2016, during which the company consolidated a long acquisition run (Super Rewards, Miva, Cubics, Lookery, Hydra Group, AdParlor, Giant Media, TriVu Media and others) into video and social units that were then sold off; AdParlor was subsequently acquired by Fluent in 2019. Third-party company registries now list Adknowledge as out of business. It entered the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub via kleiner-perkins. Contemporary integration write-ups confirm a historical RESTful AdStation / Publisher Platform API, but as of this enrichment pass no live surface survives: the adknowledge.com zone is still registered (AWS Route 53 nameservers, Microsoft 365 mail with an SPF record) yet publishes no A record for the apex or for www, api, developer, developers, docs or publisher, so there is no reachable website, developer portal, API documentation or machine-readable specification from which to harvest provider artifacts.

companies.name: Adku
companies.description: Adku was a big-data e-commerce personalization startup founded around 2010 by former Googlers (CEO Ajit Varma with co-founders Carlos Whitt and Jesse Shieh), and an AngelPad alumnus. It built machine-learning technology to personalize the online shopping experience for visitors to e-commerce sites such as eBay, Amazon, and Zappos. Backed by Battery Ventures, Greylock Partners, and True Ventures (roughly $1.49M raised), Adku was acquired by Groupon in February 2012 and is no longer an operating, independent company. It has no public developer portal, API, or documentation surface; this record is retained in the API Evangelist network as a Battery Ventures portfolio lead for historical/enrichment tracking only.

companies.name: adludio
companies.description: Adludio is an AI-powered interactive mobile advertising company founded in 2015 in London by Paul Coggins (originally Future Ad Labs). Its "Sensory Ad Science" platform builds rich, interactive mobile ad units using touch, motion and haptic interaction, sold on a cost-per-engagement rather than CPM model, with brand clients including Nike, Microsoft, Coca-Cola and Estee Lauder. The company was backed by Balderton Capital. As of 2026 the adludio.com domain 301-redirects to permate.com (an unrelated Vietnamese partnership-automation platform), indicating the original company is no longer operating a public web presence; no public API or developer surface was found during enrichment.

companies.name: AdMeld
companies.description: AdMeld was a New York City advertising-technology company founded in 2007 (by Ben Barokas and Brian Adams) that ran a supply-side platform / private ad exchange helping premium digital publishers optimize and monetize their ad inventory (serving 500+ publishers including FOX News and The Weather Channel). Google acquired AdMeld in 2011 for roughly $400M and folded its technology into the DoubleClick Ad Exchange. AdMeld no longer operates as an independent product and exposes no standalone public API; the admeld.com domain now serves a Google-maintained legacy landing page for DoubleClick Ad Exchange (Google nameservers, Google-hosted).

companies.name: AdNectar
companies.description: AdNectar was a social advertising startup founded in 2008 and headquartered in Palo Alto, California, that built a sponsored virtual-gifts network for Facebook applications and other social platforms. Its product let agencies and brands run campaigns in which consumers gave branded virtual gifts drawn from a catalog, paired with an embedded rich-media landing unit plus viral distribution, optimization, and reporting, so social-app publishers could monetize their virtual-goods inventory. The company raised roughly $5.3M from investors including Battery Ventures before being acqui-hired by Lockerz in November 2011. AdNectar is now defunct; its original adnectar.com domain is parked and serves no live product, developer portal, or public API. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead record and is not an active API provider. Note that the unrelated adnectar.io (performance marketing) and addnectar.com (Addnectar Solutions) are separate companies and are not associated with this entity.

companies.name: Adphorus
companies.description: Adphorus was an Istanbul- and Berlin-based travel marketing-science company and an official Facebook and Instagram Marketing Partner (certified since 2014) that specialized in automated, scalable Dynamic Ads for Travel, helping brands such as Expedia, Trivago, and Kayak scale full-funnel performance on Facebook and Instagram. The company was acquired by Sojern in November 2017 and subsequently absorbed; it operates no independent public website or developer API today, so this network profile is retained as a historical/portfolio record rather than an active API provider. The enrichment pipeline found no live domain, developer portal, or specification to harvest.

companies.name: Advolve.AI
companies.description: Advolve.AI is an AI-driven performance-marketing and customer-acquisition platform for e-commerce brands and marketplaces, offering an end-to-end solution to automate, scale, and optimize paid media and digital advertising, including a patent-pending creative-optimization capability that tunes interactive ad elements (messaging, graphics, colors, fonts). Founded in 2023 and headquartered in Sao Paulo, Brazil, Advolve was backed by Prosus Ventures and Valor Capital and was acquired by iFood (Prosus group) in November 2025 to power iFood Ads across Latin America. Advolve publishes a marketing website only; as of enrichment it exposes no public developer program, API, SDKs, or documentation surface.

companies.name: Aiden.ai
companies.description: Aiden.ai was a London-based marketing-analytics startup, founded in 2016 by Marie Outtier and Pierre-Jean Camillieri, that built what it billed as the first AI-powered marketing analyst: a machine-reading assistant that ingested large volumes of paid-advertising data to surface actionable insights, detect anomalies, predict campaign performance, and proactively act to improve ROI. It raised a $1.6M seed round led by Partech in 2018 and was acquired by Twitter (now X) on 2019-11-21. The company no longer operates as an independent business, ships no public product or developer API, and the aiden.ai domain is now parked and listed for sale (Afternic). This profile is retained as a Partech portfolio lead but is defunct: there is no live developer surface to enrich.

companies.name: AirKit
companies.description: AirKit (Airkit.ai) was a low-code platform for building customer-facing digital experiences and, later, AI-powered customer service agents, backed by Accel and Emergence Capital. The company was acquired by Salesforce (announced 2023) and its technology now underpins Salesforce Agentforce. As of this enrichment pass, www.airkit.com 301-redirects to salesforce.com/agentforce and the domain's CAA records point to salesforce.com, so AirKit no longer operates an independent developer surface, API, documentation, or portal of its own — all first-party discovery URLs resolve into Salesforce properties. This profile is retained as an acquired-company record; enrichment beyond domain-level DNS/TLS evidence is not applicable.

companies.name: appconomy
companies.description: Appconomy was a mobile-commerce platform company, founded in 2010 and dual-headquartered in Austin, Texas and Shanghai, China, that let brands, retailers, service providers, and mobile carriers add commerce functionality (daily deals, coupons, loyalty and rewards, mobile gifting, and merchant app generation for marketplaces such as Taobao) to their mobile apps. It was venture-backed with strategic investors including Qiming Venture Partners (lead of a $10M Series A), True Ventures, Neusoft Holdings, and WTI. The company is now permanently closed and publishes no live developer surface. The appconomy.cn domain does not resolve, appconomy.com returns 404, and no public API, documentation, developer portal, SDK, or /.well-known/ endpoint could be found. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-graph record rather than an active API provider.

companies.name: Apsalar
companies.description: Apsalar was a mobile marketing analytics and attribution company (founded 2010, headquartered in San Francisco, backed by Battery Ventures and 500 Startups/500 Global) that provided a mobile measurement platform (MMP) for app install attribution, campaign analytics, and marketing data unification. In 2017 Apsalar merged into Singular (singular.net); the Apsalar brand and its developer/API surface were retired as part of that acquisition. The apsalar.com apex domain no longer resolves to a live site and www.apsalar.com now redirects to Singular, so there is no active first-party API, OpenAPI, or developer portal to enrich. This profile is retained as an acquired-company lead pointing to its successor, Singular.

companies.name: Auditude
companies.description: Auditude was a Palo Alto video advertising technology company founded in 2007 that let premium publishers, content owners and media companies manage, serve and monetize advertising around online video across multiple platforms and devices via its proprietary Auditude Connect platform. Backed by Redpoint Ventures and Greylock Partners with roughly $38M raised, its customers included Comcast, Sony Music and Universal Music Group. Adobe acquired Auditude in November 2011 for a reported ~$120M and folded the technology into Adobe Primetime (ad decisioning / ad insertion), since rebranded under Adobe Pass. Auditude no longer operates as an independent company: auditude.com does not resolve, and the only surviving public footprint is the legacy com.auditude.ads.* namespace inside Adobe's Primetime Player SDK documentation. This profile is retained as a defunct / acquired historical record; there is no Auditude API surface to catalog.

companies.name: Augur
companies.description: Augur, Inc. was a Boulder, Colorado startup (founded 2012) that offered a cross-device attribution API using machine learning to recognize a unique device and its owner across laptops, phones, and tablets without relying on cookies, serving ad-tech and security customers to personalize experiences and improve conversion. Techstars-backed (also iGan Partners and Right Side Capital), Augur raised roughly $1.16M before being acquired by Wunderkind (formerly Bounce Exchange / BounceX) on 2017-05-04. The augur.io domain no longer resolves to a live product origin (Cloudflare edge returns HTTP 522) and no developer portal, API reference, or SDKs remain publicly reachable, so this profile is retained as an inactive/acquired historical record rather than a live API provider.

companies.name: Azarus
companies.description: Azarus was a consumer startup that built an interactive engagement and rewards layer for live game streaming and esports, letting viewers take part in real-time interactive experiences and earn blockchain-based crypto rewards while watching streams on platforms like Twitch. Backed by Kleiner Perkins, Azarus was acquired by Coinbase in April 2021 to build interactive experiences into its consumer products. The former azarus.io domain now 302-redirects to a YouTube video and exposes no public API, developer portal, documentation, packages, or other machine-readable surface; this profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead with no live API to enrich.

companies.name: Baker Technologies
companies.description: Baker Technologies (Baker) was a Denver, Colorado based customer relationship management (CRM) and marketing platform built for the cannabis industry, founded in 2014 by David Champion, Joel Milton, and Roger Obando. A graduate of the 500 Startups accelerator, Baker helped licensed dispensaries grow revenue and build customer relationships through online ordering, loyalty programs, SMS/text messaging, and analytics, and launched an expanded integrations program with a developer API connecting dispensaries to 20+ ancillary cannabis services. The company raised approximately $11.75M (including an $8M Series A) before being acquired by TILT Holdings in 2018. The trybaker.com domain is now parked and listed for sale, indicating the product has been discontinued; no live developer portal, API documentation, or specifications are publicly available.

companies.name: BankOns
companies.description: BankOns was a San Mateo, California mobile savings startup founded in the summer of 2010 by Joshua Greenough, a former VP of Operations at PowerReviews. Launched in May 2011, the app connected a user's bank transaction history to their location, analyzing spending habits to surface the nearby merchant deals and rewards best suited to them, drawing on Foursquare and other local deals data. The name was a contraction of "bank" and "coupons". BankOns was seed funded by 500 Startups (now 500 Global) plus a friends-and-family round. In May 2012 Capital One acquired select BankOns software through a limited asset purchase agreement, and several team members including Greenough joined Capital One Labs. The product was wound down and the company no longer operates a consumer service or a developer platform. The bankons.com domain resolves to a GoDaddy parking lander with no content, and no API, documentation, SDK, or developer surface exists.

companies.name: Beckon
companies.description: Beckon was a marketing analytics and marketing performance measurement SaaS platform, founded in 2011 and headquartered in San Mateo, California. Its product automated the ingestion, harmonization, and normalization of marketing data from across paid, owned, and earned channels into a single unified set of metrics and dashboards, giving marketing teams a "total marketing intelligence" view of spend, performance, and ROI. Beckon was venture-backed by Canaan Partners and Storm Ventures, and was subsequently acquired into the IgniteTech (ESW Capital / Trilogy) portfolio. The independent beckon.com domain now redirects to its acquirer, IgniteTech, and the company no longer operates a public developer program, API documentation, or developer portal of its own.

companies.name: black-unique
companies.description: Black Unique (全球购骑士特权, "Global Shopping Knight Privilege") is a membership-based consumer e-commerce and discounts platform founded in 2018 and headquartered in Guangzhou, China. Its core product is a privileges/membership card that aggregates discounts and special offers across a wide range of consumer categories: online shopping on major marketplaces such as Tmall, JD.com and Kaola, in-person shopping at international duty-free shops, outlets and supermarkets across 24-plus countries, plus dining, entertainment, travel and fuel. The company operates a consumer-facing app and website rather than a public developer program, and is backed by Qiming Venture Partners along with CCV, Eastern Bell Venture Capital and INCE Capital. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a Qiming portfolio lead; enrichment found no public API, developer portal, SDK, or other developer surface.

companies.name: Bloomin' Brands
companies.description: Bloomin' Brands, Inc. (NASDAQ: BLMN) is one of the largest casual dining restaurant companies in the world, headquartered in Tampa, Florida and founded in 1988. It owns and operates four restaurant concepts — Outback Steakhouse, Carrabba's Italian Grill, Bonefish Grill, and Fleming's Prime Steakhouse & Wine Bar — across the United States and internationally (Brazil, South Korea, Hong Kong, and China). The company's consumer technology centers on the Web-based Dine Rewards loyalty program, per-brand mobile apps (iOS/Android) for online ordering, curbside takeaway, delivery, table payment, reservations, and waitlist, and corporate supplier portals (BBI Connect). Bloomin' Brands does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a developer portal; the apis collection below is intentionally empty.

companies.name: Blue Kai
companies.description: Blue Kai (BlueKai) was a cloud-based big-data and data management platform (DMP) for audience, marketing, and advertising data, founded in 2008 and backed by Battery Ventures. Oracle acquired BlueKai in 2014 and folded it into Oracle Data Cloud / Oracle Advertising; the bluekai.com domain now 301-redirects to oracle.com (verified 2026-07-18, HTTP 403 at www.oracle.com). No independent Blue Kai developer portal, API, OpenAPI, documentation, changelog, or event surface remains, so no live provider API artifacts can be enriched. This record is retained as an acquired-company / VC-portfolio node rather than an active API provider.

companies.name: Bluebirds
companies.description: Bluebirds is an AI-powered outbound sales and go-to-market (GTM) prospecting platform, founded in 2022 by Rohan Punamia (CEO) and Kunal Punera (CTO). The product helps sales teams create, test, and scale AI-driven prospecting triggers, letting representatives target and personalize outreach in a unified workflow so they reach the right personas with the right message at the right time. Bluebirds was seed-funded by Lightspeed Venture Partners (invested 2023). As of July 2026 the primary domain bluebirds.com 301-redirects to Salesforce's AI prospecting agent page, indicating the Bluebirds team and technology have been absorbed into Salesforce. Bluebirds exposes no public developer or API surface — no docs, developer, api, status, or trust subdomains resolve, and the application host (app.bluebirds.com) is login-gated behind bot protection — so this profile is identity-only and carries no API artifacts.

companies.name: Bluefin Labs
companies.description: Bluefin Labs was a social TV analytics company founded in 2008 in Cambridge, Massachusetts by Deb Roy and Michael Fleischman, spun out of research at the MIT Media Lab. Its platform semantically interpreted public social media commentary from Twitter, Facebook and blogs and automatically linked those comments to the television shows and advertisements people were watching, producing audience engagement measurement for networks, agencies and brands. Its product, Bluefin Signals, gave media buyers a tool for accessing and analyzing social TV response data. The company raised a Series A led by Redpoint Ventures in 2010 and a $12M Series B led by Time Warner Investments in January 2012, with SoftBank Capital and Lerer Ventures participating. Twitter acquired Bluefin Labs on February 6, 2013 for a reported ~$100 million and absorbed the team and technology into its TV advertising and analytics products. The company is DEFUNCT: it operates no independent product, developer program or API, and the bluefinlabs.com domain no longer belongs to the company — it now redirects to an unrelated news site. This profile is retained as a historical / portfolio-graph record only.

companies.name: BlueKai
companies.description: BlueKai was a data management platform (DMP) and third-party audience data marketplace founded in 2008 that let marketers collect, organize, and activate first- and third-party audience data for programmatic advertising and targeting. Oracle acquired BlueKai in 2014 and folded it into the Oracle Data Cloud; Oracle wound down its advertising business (including the former BlueKai and Data Cloud assets) in 2024. The company operates no independent developer program today — the bluekai.com domain 301-redirects to Oracle's advertising pages and exposes no live public API surface. This profile is retained as a historical/defunct provider record in the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: BoomTrain
companies.description: BoomTrain was a machine-learning marketing technology startup that used AI to power personalized, cross-channel messaging (email, web, and push notifications) for brands, predicting individual content and send-time recommendations for each consumer. Backed by 500 Global (formerly 500 Startups) among others, BoomTrain raised roughly $15M before being acquired by Zeta Global in July 2017 (reportedly $35-40M), which folded its machine-learning, decisioning, and personalization technology into the Zeta Marketing Platform. The boomtrain.com domain now redirects to Zeta Global; there is no standalone BoomTrain developer portal, public API, or documentation surface. This profile is retained as a historical company record in the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Boost Media
companies.description: Boost Media (formerly BoostCTR) was a digital-advertising creative-optimization SaaS platform that paired machine-learning analysis with a curated marketplace of more than 1,000 human writers and designers to test and improve ad creative across paid search, social, video, and display campaigns. Its technology powered roughly $1 billion in paid-search advertising for around 100 global brands across retail, education, financial services, healthcare and insurance, gaming, auto, and travel. Backed by Battery Ventures (Series C, $19M, 2014), Founder Collective, and 500 Global, the company raised about $42.8M total before being acquired by AdLabs Technology in April 2019. The company is now closed and its former domain (boostmedia.com) no longer resolves; this profile is retained as a Battery Ventures portfolio record. No public API, developer portal, or specification surface exists to enrich.

companies.name: Brainient
companies.description: Brainient was a London-based advertising technology company founded in 2009 by Emi Gal that specialized in interactive video advertising and Dynamic Creative Optimization (DCO). Its platform made online video ads more personalized and interactive by matching creative to real-time context such as socio-demographics, geolocation, device, time of day, and weather. Brainient was acquired by Teads in September 2016 and folded into the Teads Studio division; the standalone Brainient brand and its brainient.com domain are now defunct. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. No public API surface, developer documentation, or machine-readable specification was located for Brainient during enrichment.

companies.name: Bravado
companies.description: Bravado is a community platform for sales professionals, best known as the War Room, which it describes as the world's largest online sales community with more than 400,000 members. Founded in 2016 and headquartered in San Francisco, Bravado offers career networking, anonymous peer Q&A, a jobs and hiring marketplace that matches sales talent with companies, an AI recruiter called Hunter, and a virtual "commission points" rewards currency, delivered through the web and a mobile app. The company is backed by Redpoint Ventures. Bravado does not publish a public developer API; its product is built on an internal GraphQL backend. As of this profile's enrichment date the primary domain bravado.co resolves to a Gandi parking page ("this domain name is unavailable") and is not serving the live product.

companies.name: BrightFunnel
companies.description: BrightFunnel was a San Francisco-based B2B marketing analytics company founded in 2012 that built a revenue attribution and forecasting platform. Its Revenue Intelligence Suite gave B2B marketers multi-touch attribution, revenue-funnel analysis, account-based measurement, web analytics, and predictive forecasting so they could quantify marketing's impact on pipeline and revenue and align plans with business priorities. BrightFunnel was acquired by account-based marketing vendor Terminus in January 2018, and its multi-channel analytics were folded into the Terminus platform.
