It no longer operates as a standalone product: the brightfunnel.com domain now serves only a redirect, and there is no live developer portal, public API, documentation, SDK, or discovery surface (.well-known, llms.txt) to enrich. This profile remains a historical company stub, originally surfaced as a portfolio company of bloomberg-beta.

companies.name: BrightRoll
companies.description: BrightRoll was a programmatic video advertising platform founded in 2006 in San Francisco that ran one of the largest independent real-time bidding marketplaces for digital video ads (RTB/DSP/SSP), connecting brand advertisers and agencies with publisher video inventory across web, mobile, and connected devices. The company was acquired by Yahoo in November 2014 and its technology was folded into Yahoo's advertising stack, later branded under Oath / Verizon Media and now Yahoo Advertising. BrightRoll no longer operates as an independent provider and publishes no standalone developer program or public API. As of this enrichment pass its former domain, brightroll.com, returns an HTTP 301 redirect to Yahoo's advertising platforms page, and the domain is served from Yahoo-owned DNS and mail infrastructure. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an acquired / absorbed company record rather than an active API producer.

companies.name: Buddy Media
companies.description: Buddy Media was a social media marketing and advertising platform (founded 2007, backed by ggv-capital, insight-partners and ivp) that helped brands manage publishing, engagement and paid campaigns across Facebook, Twitter and other social networks. It was acquired by Salesforce in 2012 and folded into the Salesforce Marketing Cloud (Social Studio) product line; the buddymedia.com domain now redirects to salesforce.com/marketing. No standalone Buddy Media public API, developer portal or first-party SDK remains — this network entry is retained as a historical martech company stub.

companies.name: Buysight
companies.description: Buysight, Inc. was a Silicon Valley advertising technology startup founded in 2008 that built intent-based audience targeting, retargeting, and Dynamic Creative Optimization (DCO) for display advertising, using machine learning to select both the audience for an impression and the creative shown to that user. The company raised approximately $16 million from ONSET Ventures, Rembrandt Venture Partners, Uncork Capital (SoftTech VC / Jeff Clavier), Reid Hoffman, and AOL. On December 4, 2012 Buysight was acquired by AOL's Advertising.com Group, with the entire team joining AOL and the DCO and machine-learning technology folded into AOL's AdLearn optimization engine alongside Advertising.com, ADTECH, the AOL On Network, goviral, and Pictela. Buysight no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no developer program, API, documentation, or SDKs. The buysight.com domain is held by MarkMonitor and redirects to a registrar placeholder page. This profile is retained as a historical acquisition record in the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: BYBE
companies.description: BYBE, Inc. is a promotion platform for the beer, wine, and spirits industry, connecting alcohol beverage brands, retailers, and consumers through digital rebates and promotional offers. Backed by Techstars, BYBE operates in the regulated alcohol marketing space where compliance and channel constraints shape how promotions reach shoppers. As of this profile the company publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable specification; this record captures its identity plus a live domain-security probe.

companies.name: Callidus Software
companies.description: Callidus Software Inc. (branded CallidusCloud) was an enterprise SaaS provider of sales performance and lead-to-money solutions, including Enterprise Incentive Management (EIM) / sales commissions, configure-price-quote (CPQ), contract lifecycle management (CLM), marketing automation, sales enablement, learning management, and gamification. Incorporated in Delaware in 1996 and headquartered in Dublin, California, it went public on Nasdaq (CALD) in 2003. SAP acquired CallidusCloud for $2.4 billion in January 2018, rebranded parts of it (e.g. SAP Litmos for the learning suite), delisted the company, and later divested pieces in 2022. As an independent developer surface CallidusCloud is defunct — the former docs portal (docs.calliduscloud.com) no longer serves a valid TLS certificate and calliduscloud.com now redirects to SAP's acquired-brands page.

companies.name: Campanja
companies.description: Campanja was a Stockholm-based advertising-technology company founded in 2010 that built a high-frequency paid-search bid-optimization engine. Its platform placed millions of automated bids per day across Google AdWords, Google Shopping, and Yahoo/Bing search campaigns, using real-time tracking and predictive big-data modeling to improve return on ad spend for large online advertisers while cutting media cost. Campanja raised a $5M Series A (Hoxton Ventures, DFJ Esprit) and was acquired by [24]7.ai in 2015, where its technology was folded into the [24]7 Customer Acquisition Cloud. The independent company is effectively defunct and campanja.com no longer resolves to a live site. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio lead and processed by the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline.

companies.name: Canopy Labs
companies.description: Canopy Labs was a customer analytics and predictive marketing SaaS company founded in 2012 in the Toronto, Ontario area (Thornhill) by Wojciech Gryc and Jorge Escobedo, with an additional office in San Francisco. A Y Combinator alumnus, it built machine-learning software that helped businesses model and predict customer behavior, optimize purchase funnels, and personalize marketing across the customer journey. The company raised seed funding from investors including BDC Venture Capital's IT Fund and Valar Ventures. In 2018 Canopy Labs was acquired by Drop Technologies (the customer-loyalty app Drop), after which the independent product, website (canopylabs.com), and any developer/API surface were wound down. This profile is retained as a historical company record; the entity no longer operates independently and publishes no live API.

companies.name: chatail
companies.description: Chatail is a Shanghai-based SaaS company (founded 2016) that provides private-domain livestream and video sales software for high-end and luxury retail brands across fashion, jewelry, beauty, automotive, and home-goods verticals, pairing intelligent customer acquisition with conversion tooling ("智能获客与高效转化双轮驱动"). The product is delivered as a hosted web application at chatail.com; no public developer API, documentation portal, or OpenAPI surface is published at this time (api.chatail.com serves a default nginx placeholder). Chatail raised a Series B round led by Qiming Venture Partners and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a Qiming portfolio company.

companies.name: Chordiant Software
companies.description: Chordiant Software Corporation was an enterprise software vendor founded in 1991 and based in California, known for customer relationship management (CRM) and customer decision management software used by large banks, insurers, telecommunications carriers, and healthcare organizations. Its products included Chordiant Decision Management, Marketing Director, and Recommendation Advisor, delivering real-time predictive decisioning and next-best-action recommendations across customer channels. The company went public on NASDAQ (CHRD) in 2000 and was acquired by Pegasystems in 2010, with its decisioning technology folded into Pega's Customer Decision Hub. Chordiant no longer operates as an independent company and exposes no public developer portal or API; the chordiant.com domain now redirects to pega.com. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead record and carries no live API surface to enrich.

companies.name: Chute
companies.description: Chute was a visual marketing automation platform (getchute.com) that helped brands discover, collect, rights-manage and publish consumer and user-generated visual content. Its product line spanned visual insights, digital asset management and content publishing, and it exposed a public REST API documented on Apiary (docs.chute.apiary.io) with first-party Ruby and Node.js client libraries. The company is defunct: the canonical domain no longer serves a site, the API and developer hosts do not resolve, the Apiary documentation returns 502, and the github.com/chute organization has been deleted. Only the abandoned package-registry entries survive. Retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical record of a former API provider.

companies.name: Cogito
companies.description: Cogito Corp was a Boston-based real-time artificial-intelligence company that provided emotional-intelligence and conversation-guidance software for contact-center agents, analyzing voice signals during live phone calls to coach agents in the moment and surface customer-experience and agent-wellbeing insights. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead (backed by Battery Ventures), Cogito's primary domain cogitocorp.com now 301-redirects to verint.com and its developer subdomains no longer resolve, reflecting the product's absorption into Verint's customer- experience automation portfolio. Cogito no longer operates an independent public developer or API surface; this record is retained as an identity and acquisition profile. The enrichment pass found no standalone Cogito public API, OpenAPI, documentation, developer portal, SDK, or well-known surface to catalog.

companies.name: Conteller
companies.description: Conteller is a user-generated content (UGC) marketplace where brands pay for authentic media directly from their own customers and everyday, non-famous creators. Brands publish media briefs and the platform lets creators capture, submit, and store photos, videos, and TikTok-style content, then handles paying those creators for approved submissions. A Mexican/Spanish startup (Madrid) selected for Batch 19 of 500 Global's Somos Lucha accelerator program in Latin America, Conteller has run pilots spanning roughly 1,400 creators and a dozen brands. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead of 500 Global. As of this profile the public site is a disabled Vercel deployment and no public developer portal, API, or documentation surface has been found.

companies.name: Convertro, Inc.
companies.description: Convertro, Inc. was a marketing analytics company based in Santa Monica, California, providing a multi-touch attribution platform that measured the ROI of marketing touchpoints across online and offline media using algorithmic attribution models. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, Convertro was acquired by AOL in 2014 and folded into the AOL/Verizon (now Yahoo) advertising stack. It no longer operates an independent public developer surface: convertro.com redirects to yahooinc.com, and no developer portal, documentation, API, or reachable API host was found during enrichment. This profile is retained as a network record; there is no live provider API surface to enrich.

companies.name: coohua
companies.description: Coohua (酷划在线) is a Beijing-based Chinese mobile advertising company founded in 2014 and backed by Qiming Venture Partners. It pioneered the incentive- and lock-screen-advertising model in China, rewarding users with cash for unlocking their screens, reading content, and engaging with ads. Its flagship products include Coohua Lockscreen (酷划锁屏) and the Tao News (淘新闻) reading-rewards app, serving advertisers across internet, finance, automotive, and e-commerce verticals. At its peak Coohua captured a majority share of China's lock-screen advertising market and returned billions of yuan in cash rewards to users annually. No public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification could be found during enrichment; this profile is retained as a company/provider record surfaced from the Qiming portfolio.

companies.name: CrowdMob
companies.description: CrowdMob was a mobile gaming and app-monetization startup surfaced as an a16z portfolio company. Enrichment probing on 2026-07-20 found no operating API surface: the company no longer appears in the a16z portfolio listing, and the crowdmob.com domain is now operated by an unrelated affiliate-marketing publisher (AffiliateBay) as a WordPress "growth marketing agency" landing page. No developer portal, documentation, API reference, specs, SDKs, packages, or /.well-known/ discovery documents exist. Retained as a historical/defunct record rather than an active API provider.

companies.name: Customer Database
companies.description: Customer Database is the topic dedicated to APIs, schemas, vocabularies, and reference designs for the systems of record that store customer identity, profile, contact, preference, consent, and account data. A customer database underpins CRM, marketing automation, customer data platforms (CDPs), customer service, billing, and analytics use cases, and is increasingly expected to support API-first access, schema-on-write data quality, real-time eventing, GDPR/CCPA consent and erasure workflows, and identity resolution across web, mobile, and offline channels. This repository tracks the vendors, standards, and patterns that make customer data accessible, governed, and portable.

companies.name: DAOex
companies.description: DAOex (DAO Exchange, product-branded "Commune") was a web3 community relationship management platform positioned as an all-in-one tool for understanding, engaging, and growing DAO and NFT communities. Its advertised surface covered member directories bridging on-chain and off-chain data, referral programs with unique member/affiliate links, quests, contests and bounties as rewards infrastructure, Discord-native engagement and role assignment, and payouts of tokens, NFTs or Discord roles on Ethereum mainnet and Polygon via an automatically provisioned Gnosis Safe, with a points-and-CSV fallback for pre-token communities. Surfaced as a portfolio company of multicoin-capital. As of the 2026-07-20 enrichment pass the company appears DEFUNCT: daoex.app no longer resolves in DNS (NXDOMAIN, no SOA), the site was a single-page Webflow marketing site last published 2022-09-22 and last archived 2023-03-21, and no API, developer portal, documentation, SDK, package or GitHub organization was ever published.

companies.name: Dapper
companies.description: Dapper was an advertising-technology and web-data company founded in 2006 by Jonathan Aizen and Eran Shir, seed-funded by Accel. It ran two surfaces: Dapper Ads, an intent-driven dynamic-ad product that pulled live product and inventory data from an advertiser's own site into targeted creative without IT integration; and open.dapper.net (the "Dapp Factory" / Dapper: The Data Mapper), a hosted tool that turned any web page into structured feeds, web services and widgets — XML, RSS, JSON, YAML, CSV, iCalendar, Google Gadgets, Netvibes modules and image loops — effectively letting anyone "create an API for any site" before providers published their own. Dapper was acquired by Yahoo! in 2010 and both surfaces were shut down; dapper.net now resolves to Yahoo nameservers with no host, and open.dapper.net no longer resolves. There is no live API, developer portal, or documentation to enrich.

companies.name: DataFox
companies.description: DataFox was a San Francisco company-intelligence and sales-prospecting startup, backed by GV among others, that used machine learning to collect and score signals about private and public companies (funding rounds, hiring, news, growth signals) and delivered them to sales and marketing teams through a web application, CRM integrations, and a company-data API. Oracle acquired DataFox and folded its company-and-signals data into the Oracle Cloud CX / Oracle Fusion Marketing stack. The independent product has been fully retired: as of this profile the datafox.com apex and www hosts are served from Oracle infrastructure and every path under www.datafox.com issues a blanket HTTP 301 to Oracle marketing pages, while api.datafox.com and app.datafox.com resolve to a parked Oracle address that accepts no connections. There is no surviving DataFox developer portal, documentation, API reference, or specification to harvest, so this profile is retained as a historical/acquired company record rather than an active API provider.

companies.name: Datalogix
companies.description: Datalogix was a consumer-purchase and marketing data company that connected offline buying behavior to digital advertising audiences, enabling measurement and targeting for brands and ad platforms. Backed by General Catalyst and IVP, it was acquired by Oracle in 2014 and folded into the Oracle Data Cloud. The datalogix.com domain now 301-redirects to Oracle's acquisitions page, and no standalone Datalogix developer portal, API, or documentation remains publicly available.

companies.name: DataSine
companies.description: DataSine was a London-based AI personalization startup, founded in 2015 and backed by Techstars, that applied machine learning and behavioral psychology to help marketers tailor content, imagery, and copy to audience personality traits. The company was acquired by Shutterstock and folded into Shutterstock's AI/creative-intelligence work; its datasine.com domain is now registered to Shutterstock, Inc. (MarkMonitor) and HTTP 301-redirects to shutterstock.ai. DataSine no longer operates an independent product or a developer/API surface, so this profile is retained as an acquired-company record rather than an active provider awaiting API artifacts.

companies.name: Dataxu
companies.description: DataXu was a Boston-based programmatic advertising technology company, founded in 2009, that built a cloud-based demand-side platform (DSP) for automated, data-driven media buying across display, video, mobile, and connected TV. The company was acquired by Roku in 2019 and its technology was absorbed into Roku's OneView advertising platform (now Roku Ads). DataXu no longer operates as an independent brand: its primary domain (dataxu.com) 301-redirects into Roku's advertising site, and there is no independent DataXu developer portal, public API, SDK, or documentation surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical / acquired-company record surfaced from the Menlo Ventures portfolio.

companies.name: Datorama
companies.description: Datorama was a cloud-based marketing intelligence and analytics platform founded in 2012 in Tel Aviv and New York. It unified marketing, advertising, and sales data from thousands of disparate sources into a single AI-powered reporting and dashboarding layer, using its "Genius" machine-learning engine to automate data harmonization across ad, social, web, and CRM APIs. Salesforce acquired Datorama in August 2018 for a reported ~$800 million and rebranded it as Salesforce Marketing Cloud Intelligence (Marketing Intelligence). The standalone datorama.com domain now 301-redirects to the Salesforce Marketing Intelligence product page, and the former standalone developer/API surface has been folded into Salesforce documentation. This profile entered the API Evangelist network as a lightspeed-venture-partners portfolio lead.

companies.name: Digby
companies.description: Digby was an Austin, Texas software-as-a-service provider of mobile commerce and mobile engagement solutions for large retailers, operating under parent company 30 Second Software Inc. Its platform — including the Localpoint location-based marketing product — delivered branded mobile web experiences and native shopping apps, connecting digital engagement to physical stores for customers such as Cabela's, Kohl's, Catalina Marketing and Hasbro. Digby raised venture funding from Battery Ventures, S3 Ventures, Daylight Ventures, Relay Ventures and the BlackBerry Partners Fund. The company was acquired by fellow Austin mobile company Phunware in May 2014 (along with its Movaya subsidiary in Seattle and Chengdu), terms undisclosed, and the Localpoint technology was folded into Phunware's product line. Digby no longer operates as an independent company: digby.com no longer resolves to a live site (last Internet Archive capture February 2015) and there is no current developer portal, documentation, API, SDK or other public API surface to catalog.

companies.name: Digital Room
companies.description: Digital Room is a marketing and printing services company that for nearly three decades has helped small and medium-sized businesses reach customers, promote products, and build their brands. It operates a family of online printing and marketing brands serving SMBs with print, signage, and promotional products. Backed by Insight Partners, it was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture.

companies.name: Direct Revenue
companies.description: Direct Revenue was surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub lead. A July 2026 enrichment pass found no live corporate or developer surface for this company: directrevenue.com resolves to an Efty domain-for-sale parking lander (domain registered 2002, held at Tucows, listed for sale); direct-revenue.com is a squatted domain that 302-redirects to baidu.com; directrevenue.co returns Cloudflare 522 (origin unreachable); and directrevenue.net, directrevenue.ai and getdirectrevenue.com do not resolve at all. There is no website, no developer portal, no documentation, no API, and no matching provider in the APIs.io catalog. This profile is retained as a historical lead record only and carries no API artifacts.

companies.name: Double Click
companies.description: DoubleClick was an interactive marketing and advertising technology company founded in 1996 by Kevin O'Connor and Dwight Merriman. It pioneered ad serving, targeting, and campaign measurement for publishers and advertisers, went public on NASDAQ as DCLK, and was acquired by Google in 2008 for roughly $3.1 billion. Its products were folded into Google's advertising stack — DoubleClick for Publishers became Google Ad Manager and DoubleClick Digital Marketing became the Google Marketing Platform. DoubleClick no longer exists as an independent company or API provider; doubleclick.com now redirects to Google Marketing Platform. This API Evangelist profile is retained as a historical venture-portfolio record (surfaced via lightspeed-venture-partners) rather than a live, enrichable developer surface.

companies.name: Drawbridge
companies.description: Drawbridge, Inc. was a San Mateo, California cross-device identity and digital advertising company founded in 2011 by Kamakshi Sivaramakrishnan (a former AdMob scientist). It built a people-based identity graph that used machine learning to probabilistically match individuals across their connected devices (desktops, smartphones, tablets, and connected TVs) so brands could serve and measure relevant advertising across devices. Backed by Kleiner Perkins, Sequoia Capital, Northgate Capital, and Mitsui & Co., the company raised roughly $69M across five rounds before it was acquired by LinkedIn in 2019 and folded into LinkedIn Marketing Solutions. Drawbridge no longer operates as an independent company and never published a public developer API or developer portal, so there is no live API surface to enrich; this profile records its identity as a historical Kleiner Perkins portfolio company.

companies.name: Ebates
companies.description: Ebates is a consumer cash-back and rebate shopping platform founded in 2000 in San Francisco that pays members a percentage of their purchases back as cash when they shop through its links at thousands of partner retailers. Rakuten acquired Ebates in 2014 and rebranded the U.S. service as Rakuten Rewards in 2019; the ebates.com domain now redirects to rakuten.com. The business is a consumer-facing rewards and affiliate-commerce brand and does not operate an independent public developer API program. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

companies.name: Echopass
companies.description: Echopass Corporation was a cloud-based (on-demand / hosted) contact center technology company, headquartered in the San Francisco Bay Area (San Ramon / Pleasanton, California) and backed by Canaan Partners among other venture investors. Its platform delivered multichannel, carrier-grade contact center and customer-interaction capabilities as a hosted service to enterprises. Echopass was acquired by Genesys in 2013 and folded into the Genesys customer-experience portfolio; it no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no live developer, API, or documentation surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network for lineage and portfolio-graph purposes rather than as an active API provider.

companies.name: Efficient Frontier
companies.description: Efficient Frontier was a digital advertising optimization and search marketing company founded in 2002 that applied algorithmic, finance-inspired bid optimization to manage over $1 billion in annual marketing spend across search, display, and social (notably Facebook ad buying) for enterprise clients such as Discover, Travelodge, and Match.com. Adobe acquired the company in late 2011 (announced November 30, 2011; completed January 2012) and folded its multi-channel ad forecasting, execution, and optimization capabilities into the Adobe Digital Marketing / Advertising Cloud. The efrontier.com domain now redirects to adobe.com and the company has no independent website, developer portal, or public API.

companies.name: Endeavor
companies.description: Endeavor was a global sports and entertainment company representing talent and owning and operating events, with subsidiaries including WME, IMG, and UFC. Following the 2024 take-private transaction by Silver Lake and the separation of TKO Group Holdings (UFC and WWE), the remaining talent, media, marketing, and licensing businesses were rebranded as WME Group. This repository tracks Endeavor as a corporate entity; no public developer APIs are currently published.

companies.name: Endeavor Group Holdings
companies.description: Endeavor Group Holdings was a global sports and entertainment company that represented talent, owned and operated events, and provided licensing, marketing, and media services through subsidiaries including WME, IMG, and UFC. Following the 2024 take-private transaction by Silver Lake and the separation of TKO Group Holdings (UFC and WWE), the remaining talent representation, media, marketing, and licensing businesses were rebranded as WME Group, which now operates WME, 160over90, Pantheon Media Group, and IMG Licensing. No public developer APIs are currently published.

companies.name: Enghouse
companies.description: Enghouse Systems Limited (TSX: ENGH) is a publicly traded Canadian enterprise software and services company headquartered in Markham, Ontario and founded in 1984. It builds mission-critical, communications-focused software delivered on-premise and via the cloud, organized into two segments: the Interactive Management Group (Enghouse Interactive — omnichannel contact centre, customer experience, IVR, video collaboration and AI-assisted agent tooling) and the Asset Management Group (Enghouse Networks — telecom OSS/BSS, media and broadcast, and network monitoring; plus transportation, public-safety and transit systems). The company grows largely through acquisition of specialized software brands.

companies.name: Exact Target
companies.description: ExactTarget was a digital marketing and email-marketing automation SaaS company founded in 2000 in Indianapolis, Indiana. It built the Fuel developer platform and Interactive Marketing Hub for email, mobile, and social campaign automation, went public on the NYSE (ticker ET) in March 2012, and was acquired by Salesforce in December 2013 for approximately 2.5 billion dollars. ExactTarget became the foundation of Salesforce Marketing Cloud; the exacttarget.com domain now redirects to the Salesforce Marketing Cloud email-marketing product and the former developer.exacttarget.com Fuel/Code@ API platform (REST and SOAP APIs) has been retired and folded into the Salesforce Marketing Cloud developer surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical/acquired-company record.

companies.name: ExactTarget
companies.description: ExactTarget was an email and digital marketing SaaS company founded in 2000 in Indianapolis that IPO'd in 2012 and was acquired by Salesforce in 2013 for roughly $2.5 billion. Its "Fuel" developer platform and the ExactTarget API (SOAP plus REST, covering email, subscribers, triggered sends, data extensions and journeys) became the technical core of what is now the Salesforce Marketing Cloud API. The ExactTarget brand and its exacttarget.com domain are fully retired: the domain 301-redirects to Salesforce Marketing Cloud, and there is no independent ExactTarget developer portal, documentation, or live API surface to enrich. This profile is retained as a historical company record; any live API work belongs under the Salesforce Marketing Cloud successor.

companies.name: Eyeview
companies.description: Eyeview (Eyeview Digital) was a New York-based personalized and programmatic video advertising technology company, surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of lightspeed-venture-partners. As of this enrichment pass the company appears defunct - its primary domain (eyeviewdigital.com) is registered on AWS nameservers but serves no website (no DNS A record) and no email (no MX record), and no developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or public GitHub spec surface could be located. No API artifacts could be harvested; this remains a defunct-company stub.

companies.name: Fanbridge
companies.description: FanBridge was an email and SMS marketing platform for musicians, artists, bands, and creators, letting them grow and message their fan mailing lists, run newsletters, and capture subscribers from shows and social channels. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. Enrichment (2026-07-19) confirmed FanBridge is defunct - it was acquired by Kit (formerly ConvertKit) and ceased operations on April 11, 2022, with active accounts migrated to the Kit platform. The domain fanbridge.com now 302-redirects to kit.com/fanbridge. There is no standalone FanBridge developer API, documentation, SDK, or event surface; the developer docs linked from the destination site belong to Kit, not FanBridge.

companies.name: fanli
companies.description: fanli (返利网, fanli.com) is a Chinese cashback and shopping-rewards platform that aggregates promotions, coupons, and rebate offers across major online retailers, letting consumers earn money back on purchases they route through the site. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass, fanli.com is a live consumer-facing web property; no public developer portal, API documentation, machine-readable API definition, /.well-known discovery surface, llms.txt, or published security/vulnerability-disclosure program was found.

companies.name: FlexEngage
companies.description: FlexEngage is a retail customer-engagement company that powered transactional and triggered customer communications for retailers and brands, including digital receipts, order and shipping notifications, and omnichannel messaging across email, SMS, and print. The company was backed by Bullpen Capital and was acquired by Narvar in 2019. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced from the Bullpen Capital portfolio; the public site (www.flexengage.com) is currently served behind CloudFront and returns HTTP 403 to automated clients, so no public developer/API surface could be captured during enrichment.

companies.name: Fliptop
companies.description: Fliptop was a San Francisco-based predictive marketing and customer intelligence startup that applied data science and machine learning to CRM and marketing-automation data to score leads, predict conversion, and prioritize sales pipelines. Founded around 2009, it was acquired by LinkedIn in August 2015 and folded into LinkedIn's Sales Solutions (Sales Navigator) product. The company no longer operates as an independent entity and publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs; its former domain fliptop.com now 301-redirects to business.linkedin.com/sales-solutions. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio-company record.

companies.name: Flye
companies.description: Flye was a San Francisco social-audience and brand-marketing analytics startup (500 Global / 500 Startups Demo Day Batch 19, founded 2016) that helped brands build and understand their audiences from social data (an "audience fingerprint") and run targeted, personalized engagement campaigns using machine learning. The company appears defunct — its original domain (flye.co) has lapsed and now hosts an unrelated online-casino review/affiliate site. No developer platform, API, documentation, SDK, or other technical surface exists for this provider, so there is nothing for the enrichment pipeline to harvest without fabrication.

companies.name: Freshplum
companies.description: Freshplum was a San Francisco data-science startup (founded 2010) that built cloud-based predictive analytics for e-commerce, gauging online shopper behavior in real time to surface personalized promotional offers and discounts to visitors who might otherwise abandon a purchase. During its private alpha it was already processing over 10M requests a day. Freshplum raised roughly $1.7M from investors including DCVC and GV (Google Ventures) before being acquired by ad-targeting company TellApart in July 2014 (TellApart was in turn acquired by Twitter in 2015). The company is defunct: it ships no live product, developer portal, documentation, or public API, and the freshplum.com domain is now a parked listing offered for sale via Afternic. This profile is retained as a historical/portfolio record; there is no API surface to enrich.

companies.name: Get Satisfaction
companies.description: Get Satisfaction was a customer-community and engagement SaaS platform that gave companies a hosted online community where customers, employees, and prospects could ask questions, report problems, share ideas, and offer praise in public topic threads. Founded in 2007, it popularized the customer-powered support community model and offered widgets, community moderation, and integrations that companies embedded on their websites and product pages. Get Satisfaction was acquired by the social customer experience management company Sprinklr in 2015 and folded into Sprinklr's platform; the standalone product and its developer program have since been discontinued. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio-company record (backed by Uncork Capital); it no longer operates a live public API, developer portal, or documentation surface.

companies.name: Glintinc
companies.description: Glint (Glint Inc), founded in 2013 and headquartered in Redwood City, California, built a people-success and employee-engagement platform centered on frequent pulse surveys, engagement analytics, and manager action-planning to help organizations measure and improve employee experience. LinkedIn acquired Glint in November 2018, and the product was subsequently folded into Microsoft Viva as Viva Glint. There is no standalone Glint developer portal or public API: the former glintinc.com domain now 302-redirects to Microsoft's Viva Glint community, and the offering is delivered and documented through Microsoft Viva. This profile is retained for network lineage as a Norwest Venture Partners portfolio company that was acquired rather than an independently operating API provider.

companies.name: Graphiq
companies.description: Graphiq was a creative-technology startup founded in 2015 that set out to disrupt the traditional agency model by connecting companies with vetted graphic designers through a flexible design-subscription service. Backed by 500 Global, the company was acquired by Klingit in July 2024 and its brand folded into Klingit; the graphiq.design domain now redirects to klingit.com. Graphiq operated as a design-services marketplace and offered no public API, developer portal, or programmatic surface. This profile is retained as an acquired-company record in the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Greenfield Online
companies.description: Greenfield Online, Inc. (Nasdaq SRVY) was an independent provider of Internet-based survey solutions and online market-research panels, headquartered in Wilton, Connecticut. Founded in 1994, it pioneered online panel sampling and data collection for the marketing-research industry, went public in 2004, and grew by acquiring sampling firms worldwide (including European comparison-shopping service Ciao). Microsoft acquired the company in 2008 for roughly $486 million to obtain Ciao, then divested the survey and sampling assets to Toluna in 2009. Greenfield Online no longer operates as an independent entity and publishes no developer program, public API, or live web presence today. This record is retained as a portfolio-lead profile surfaced from the Insight Partners portfolio.

companies.name: H World Group
companies.description: H World Group Limited (formerly Huazhu Group / China Lodging Group) is one of the world's largest multi-brand hotel operators, headquartered in Shanghai, China and founded in 2005 by Ji Qi. It franchises, manages, and leases-and-operates thousands of hotels across economy-to-luxury tiers under brands including HanTing, Ji Hotel, Orange, Hi Inn, Elan, Starway, Crystal Orange, Manxin, Madison, Blossom House, CitiGO and Ni Hao, plus the upscale European Deutsche Hospitality portfolio (Steigenberger, IntercityHotel, MAXX, Jaz in the City, Zleep) and the H Rewards loyalty program. The company is dual-listed on NASDAQ (HTHT) and the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (1179). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of idg-capital and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; H World is a consumer hospitality operator and does not publish a public developer API surface.

companies.name: Habeas
companies.description: Habeas was an email reputation and deliverability services provider that helped legitimate senders monitor and manage their sending reputation to maximize inbox deliverability, using a trademark-based accreditation and safelist model to certify permission-based email. Founded in the mid-2000s and backed by Canaan Partners through a Series B round, Habeas was acquired by Return Path in 2008 (habeas.com now redirects to returnpath.com); Return Path was in turn acquired by Validity in 2019. The company is defunct as an independent brand and publishes no live public API or developer surface, so this profile is retained as a Canaan Partners portfolio-history record rather than an active API provider.

companies.name: HiCustomer
companies.description: HiCustomer (ハイカスタマー) was a Japanese Customer Success Management (CSM) SaaS built specifically for SaaS companies. Its platform aggregated customer data scattered across BI tools, CRMs, and chat tools to visualize product usage, communication history, revenue, and contract information in one place. Teams used configurable health-score rules to monitor account health across the customer lifecycle, and custom alerts to surface churn and upsell signals at the right moment, with time-series analysis to make customer-success outreach repeatable. The company also offered customer-success consulting. As of this enrichment pass the hicustomer.jp domain no longer resolves to a live site (its authoritative AWS Route 53 zone is empty) and the product appears discontinued; the last archived homepage (Oct 2024) shows only a minimal "About the company" page. No public developer API, documentation, SDK, or developer portal was ever published.

companies.name: Hitwise
companies.description: Hitwise was an online competitive-intelligence and audience-measurement company that tracked website traffic, clickstream behavior, and search-term data to help marketers benchmark share of visits, referral sources, and competitor performance across industry verticals. Originally an Australian firm, it was later owned by Experian and then Connexity. The Hitwise brand has since been retired -- as of this enrichment pass the hitwise.com domain no longer serves a live product (it returns a lapsed-host "Site is not available" page with a mismatched TLS certificate) and exposes no public developer portal, documentation, or API. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio-company lead of insight-partners; enrichment found no active API surface to catalog.

companies.name: Hyphen
companies.description: Hyphen was a mobile-first employee engagement and pulse-survey platform that let organizations collect anonymous employee feedback, run continuous sentiment surveys, and give managers analytics on engagement and culture. Founded as a 500 Global-backed startup, Hyphen was acquired by Betterworks and folded into the Betterworks Engage product line. Its original domain, gethyphen.com, now 301-redirects to betterworks.com/product/engage-overview/, and the company no longer operates an independent public developer or API surface. This profile is retained as an acquired-company lead in the API Evangelist network; the live successor product is Betterworks Engage.

companies.name: Insent.ai
companies.description: Insent.ai was a Boston-based, Techstars-backed B2B conversational marketing platform that let marketing and sales teams engage website visitors in real time with human-first chat, visitor identification, routing, and meeting booking. ZoomInfo acquired Insent in July 2021 and rebranded the product as ZoomInfo Chat; the insent.ai domain now serves ZoomInfo Chat. As a standalone company Insent.ai no longer operates its own developer portal, documentation, or public API surface, so the enrichment pipeline found no first-party API artifacts to harvest.

companies.name: Intellimize
companies.description: Intellimize was an AI-powered website optimization, personalization, and conversion-rate optimization platform (an amplify-partners portfolio company in the ai-ml sector) that let marketing teams continuously test and machine-learn the best-performing landing-page and website experience for each visitor. It was acquired by Webflow in 2024 and folded into the Webflow Optimize product; the entire intellimize.com domain now 301-redirects to webflow.com/feature/optimize. As a standalone brand Intellimize no longer operates an independent developer portal, public API, documentation, or SDK surface — enrichment therefore found no OpenAPI, packages, well-known documents, MCP server, or security/trust program of its own. Only live domain-security posture for the retained intellimize.com domain could be probed.

companies.name: Jelli
companies.description: Jelli was a programmatic advertising technology company focused on terrestrial and broadcast radio, building a real-time platform that let advertisers buy and manage radio spots programmatically across broadcast station inventory. Backed by Battery Ventures (among other investors), Jelli was acquired by iHeartMedia in 2016 and its technology went on to power programmatic and automated audio advertising. The independent Jelli brand is now defunct - the jelli.com domain 301-redirects to tritondigital.com, and no Jelli-branded developer portal, API reference, or public API host remains. This profile is retained as a portfolio-lead record; the enrichment pipeline found no live Jelli developer or API surface to harvest.

companies.name: Julu Mobile
companies.description: Julu Mobile was a Shanghai, China based mobile advertising network that served targeted, personalized ads to Chinese mobile users by analyzing mobile interactions to profile user interests. Backed by 500 Global, the company was acquired by Zhubajie on November 1, 2012 and no longer operates an independent product or developer platform. This profile was surfaced from the 500 Global portfolio and added to the API Evangelist network. As of the July 2026 enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, SDK, documentation, MCP server, or developer surface, and julumobile.com resolves to a Cloudflare block page.

companies.name: Jump Ramp Games
companies.description: Jump Ramp Games was a New York City casual mobile gaming company best known for Lucktastic, a free scratch-card, rewards, and instant-win app that launched on Android in 2014 and grew to roughly 10 million US installs across Android and iOS, consistently ranking near the top of the lifestyle category. Founded by Alex Betancur and Tony Vartanian and backed by Bullpen Capital, the company paired free-to-play casual gaming with performance-marketing and rewards technology. Jump Ramp Games was acquired by MobilityWare in September 2019, which took over the Lucktastic franchise; the jumprampgames.com domain now redirects to mobilityware.com. The company exposes no public developer, API, or documentation surface, so this profile is maintained as a company record in the API Evangelist network rather than an API provider.

companies.name: Jumptap
companies.description: Jumptap was a mobile advertising and audience-targeting platform founded in 2005 and based in Cambridge, Massachusetts. It matched ads to signals such as time of day, carrier network, site content, and device type, helping app developers acquire users and helping developers and publishers maximize ad revenue. In August 2013 Jumptap was acquired by Millennial Media (valued at roughly $210-232M in stock); Millennial Media was subsequently acquired by AOL/Verizon and folded into what is now Yahoo. Jumptap no longer operates as an independent entity and publishes no developer portal, documentation, or public API.

companies.name: Kanoodle
companies.description: Kanoodle was an online advertising network founded in 1999 by Kent Keating, specializing in search-targeted and later content-targeted (contextual) sponsored links, adding partners such as CBS MarketWatch in January 2004. In August 2006 it restructured under a new parent company, Seevast Corp - the search-advertising business kept the Kanoodle brand, the content-targeted contextual ad product was spun out as Pulse 360, and the newly acquired Moniker.com domain registrar ran as a separate unit. Listed here as an Insight Partners portfolio company, Kanoodle/Seevast is defunct and exposes no surviving public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation - the seevast.com domain now resolves to a parked-domain lander. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio lead.

companies.name: Krunch
companies.description: Krunch is an on-demand product studio that delivers product management, engineering, and marketing as a service, using AI and code to compress the build cycle for its clients. The team was accepted into the 500 Startup Accelerator program in Silicon Valley and markets prior engagements with Alibaba, Google, Camunda, New Relic, Polkadot, and Bowtie. Krunch operates as a services agency rather than an API provider - as of this enrichment pass it publishes a single-page marketing site with a Calendly booking link and no public developer portal, documentation, API reference, SDKs, or machine-readable API artifacts of any kind.

companies.name: Kyndoo
companies.description: Kyndoo Inc. was a San Francisco based influencer-marketing software platform that let brands find, connect to and work with social-media influencers. Its differentiator was audience authenticity: Kyndoo built a database of vetted influencers and published the "Kyndex" score, described as a credit score for influencers, which measured whether a following was made of real people with buying intent rather than purchased bot accounts. Around that database it sold campaign management, attribution and brand-safety tooling to brands, taking a service fee on the influencer deals brands negotiated through the platform. The company was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company. Kyndoo was acquired by CIPIO (cipio.ai) and its web property is now offline - kyndoo.com has not served a page since early 2022. Kyndoo never published a public API, developer portal or SDK, so this profile is an identity and lifecycle record rather than an API profile.

companies.name: Lattice Engines
companies.description: Lattice Engines was a predictive marketing and AI-driven B2B customer data platform that applied machine learning to first-party CRM and marketing automation data combined with external firmographic, technographic, and intent signals in order to score accounts and leads, prioritize sales outreach, and power account-based marketing programs. The company was acquired by Dun & Bradstreet in 2019 and the product was rebranded D&B Lattice before being folded into the Dun & Bradstreet Rev.Up ABX go-to-market platform. Lattice Engines no longer operates as an independent brand and publishes no developer surface of its own: as of the 2026-07-19 enrichment probe, www.lattice-engines.com returns HTTP 301 to dnb.com, the apex domain returns HTTP 403, api.lattice-engines.com returns HTTP 404, and developer./docs. subdomains do not resolve. This profile is retained as a historical record; the live successor surface is documented in the api-evangelist dun-and-bradstreet repository.

companies.name: Launchbit
companies.description: LaunchBit was an advertising startup founded in 2012 and incubated through 500 Startups, co-founded and led by CEO Elizabeth Yin. It launched as an email ad network that let B2B and software-as-a-service advertisers reach audiences through niche email newsletters, and helped publishers monetize email — a medium BuySellAds founder Todd Garland described as "pretty tricky to monetize." In March 2014 LaunchBit pivoted toward a customer-acquisition and lead-generation platform for SaaS companies. BuySellAds.com acquired LaunchBit in September 2014 for undisclosed terms, and the company no longer operates independently: as of a July 2026 probe, launchbit.com serves the BuySellAds corporate website for every path. LaunchBit published no public API, developer portal, or SDKs, so this profile is retained as a historical/acquired record rather than an active API provider.

companies.name: LeanMarket
companies.description: LeanMarket was a mobile advertising technology company headquartered in Mountain View, California, that brought real-time bidding (RTB) display advertising to small and mid-sized advertisers through a self-serve platform. Its pitch was transparency and operator control: advertisers could pull reports showing in-depth data on every mobile app and mobile website their ads appeared in — in contrast to blind ad networks — and could tweak, optimize and scale campaigns themselves through a self-serve interface with up-to-the-second reporting, rather than waiting on an account manager to make changes. The company went through the Y Combinator Summer 2012 (S12) batch and appears on the Andreessen Horowitz investment list, with seed participation also reported from Initialized Capital. LeanMarket is defunct and operates no live product, developer portal or API today; this profile is retained for historical and network completeness.

companies.name: Linkett
companies.description: Linkett is a digital out-of-home (DOOH) analytics platform for digital signage and retail displays. Its proprietary technology passively gathers audience data at the screen and reports real-time campaign performance metrics such as impressions, dwell time, and engagement, giving advertising agencies detailed client reporting and giving advertisers measurement they can tie back to return on ad spend. Linkett is headquartered in Canada with offices in Toronto and California, and was surfaced through the 500 Global portfolio. As of this enrichment pass Linkett publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable API specification, and its website is served behind a bot/CAPTCHA challenge that blocks automated retrieval.

companies.name: Loris
companies.description: Loris was an AI-powered customer service and conversation intelligence platform that analyzed voice, chat, and email interactions to surface contact drivers, sentiment shifts, and quality signals for support teams. Originally a Techstars-backed startup, Loris was acquired by Contentsquare and its product has been folded into the Contentsquare Conversation Intelligence offering. The standalone loris.ai property now 301-redirects to contentsquare.com and the company no longer publishes an independent public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an acquired-company record.

companies.name: Main Street Hub
companies.description: Main Street Hub was a marketing platform for local and small businesses, founded in Austin, Texas around 2010, that managed social media, review sites, and online customer engagement on behalf of restaurants, salons, and other Main Street merchants. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, it was acquired by GoDaddy in 2018 and folded into the GoDaddy Social product; the former mainstreethub.com domain now 301-redirects to godaddy.com/online-marketing/godaddy-social. No independent developer portal, OpenAPI, or public API surface remains, and api.mainstreethub.com does not resolve.

companies.name: Mainframe
companies.description: Mainframe (Mainframe Group, Inc.) is a software development and marketing services company building products for the decentralized finance (DeFi) ecosystem. It offers three service areas — Risk Management (protocol parameter optimization and stability), Development (DeFi and blockchain financial solutions), and Marketing (brand reach and audience engagement) — and has produced projects including Hifi, Pooled NFT, Sheet Heads, and Crown Ribbon. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and Techstars and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Mainframe publishes a Webflow marketing site only, with no public API, developer portal, documentation, or SDKs.

companies.name: Massive Dynamic
companies.description: Massive Dynamic is an AI-powered advertising platform that bills itself as "The Advertising Copilot" and "the human-AI interface for massive scale." It helps media and advertising teams coordinate large-scale digital ad campaigns by pairing an AI Analysis Copilot (automating daily analytics checks, quarterly business reviews, and Media Mix Modeling) with Execution Delegation, where an AI agent handles operational campaign setup so strategists can focus on decisions. The tool works inside existing Slack and email workflows as a conduit between strategy and activation teams, and emphasizes enterprise-grade data governance with ring-fenced customer data and an explicit commitment not to use customer data to train or improve models. The company was surfaced as a Seedcamp portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer documentation, or SDKs.

companies.name: Mavrck
companies.description: Mavrck is an influencer marketing platform, founded in Boston, that helps consumer brands and agencies discover creators, activate influencer and advocacy campaigns at scale, manage relationships and content workflows, and measure campaign performance across social channels. As of January 17, 2024 Mavrck rebranded and now operates as part of Later's influencer marketing offering (later.com). This record was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead (surfaced via Techstars) and enriched by the pipeline; probing confirms a marketing-SaaS web presence with no public developer API surface.

companies.name: Mediaspectrum
companies.description: Mediaspectrum is a cloud-based SaaS provider of multichannel advertising, content management, and publishing software for media companies and publishers. Founded in 2001 and headquartered in Miami, its platform manages the full advertising lifecycle -- proposal generation, packaging, scheduling, rating, workflow, trafficking, optimization, and billing -- alongside an integrated CRM and the ContentWatch content management system spanning print, web, mobile, video, social, and broadcast channels. The company raised a $35.8M investment from Insight Venture Partners in 2013 and counts Gannett, Dow Jones, and Trinity Mirror among its clients. No public API, developer portal, or SDKs are published as of this enrichment pass.

companies.name: MediaSpike
companies.description: MediaSpike was an AdTech startup founded in 2011 by Blake Commagere and headquartered in Mountain View, California, that built a native monetization platform for dynamic, programmatic product placement inside social, mobile, and virtual-reality games. Its API let game developers surface contextual in-game sponsorships and brand placements, and the network reportedly reached roughly 20 million unique users at its peak. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Google Ventures, CMEA Capital, 500 Startups, and others (a $5.2M Series A in November 2013), the company ceased operations around June 2017. mediaspike.com no longer hosts the product and currently serves only a "coming soon" placeholder; no live API, developer portal, or discovery surface remains.

companies.name: MightyHive
companies.description: MightyHive was a data and digital media consultancy that helped brands take control of their programmatic advertising, media buying, data strategy, and marketing technology. Founded as an independent programmatic trading and media consultancy, it was acquired by S4 Capital and rebranded to Media.Monks in August 2021; the S4 Capital operating company has since consolidated under the single "Monks" brand (monks.com). Its offerings spanned digital media transformation, campaign launch and measurement, customer data platform (CDP) work, Amazon eCommerce solutions, and marketing/AI transformation services for enterprise brands. It is a professional-services / consulting business, not an API product company: it publishes no public developer API, API documentation, developer portal, SDK, or open-source GitHub organization. Added to the API Evangelist network as an a16z-portfolio lead; enrichment confirms no API surface exists.

companies.name: Millennial Media
companies.description: Millennial Media was a mobile advertising / adtech company surfaced as a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. The enrichment probe (2026-07-20) found the company is defunct: millennialmedia.com now CNAMEs to rc.yahoo.com via AWS Global Accelerator on oath.cloud (Yahoo / Verizon Media / Oath infrastructure, consistent with the AOL acquisition of Millennial Media), and every host returns HTTP 404. There is no independent millennial-media developer portal, API, developer.* or api.* subdomain (NXDOMAIN), and no /.well-known/ or /llms.txt discovery surface. No API artifacts exist to enrich; this record is retained as a historical/company lead only.

companies.name: Moat
companies.description: Moat was an advertising measurement and analytics company, backed by Insight Venture Partners and Mayfield, that measured ad viewability, attention, and brand safety across digital and video advertising. Oracle acquired Moat in 2017 and folded it into Oracle Advertising (Oracle Moat / Oracle Data Cloud). The independent moat.com brand no longer operates a standalone developer program: www.moat.com now 301-redirects to oracle.com/advertising, and the bare moat.com host no longer negotiates TLS. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an acquired/absorbed company lead with no independent public API surface.

companies.name: Movivo
companies.description: Movivo was a London-based mobile rewards startup (500 Startups / Distro Dojo, HQ London) whose consumer app let users cover the cost of their mobile airtime and data by completing surveys, crowdsourced micro-tasks, and app installs, working with mobile operators across emerging markets. The company was surfaced as a portfolio lead of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. As of this enrichment pass the company appears defunct — movivo.com resolves to a parked GoDaddy for-sale domain, and no public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI definition, SDK, or GitHub organization could be found. This profile is retained as a network record with no API surface to enrich.

companies.name: Mporium
companies.description: Mporium (Mporium Group plc, formerly MoPowered) was a London-based, "mobile first" data-driven marketing and advertising-technology company founded in 2012. Its proprietary IMPACT platform delivered software-as-a-service that helped agencies and advertisers identify and act on consumer "micro-moments" across search, social, and display media, reacting to real-time signals from TV, news feeds, sports, financial data, and social media to optimise ad pricing, timing, and selection. The group also acquired the digital agency Fast Web Media. Mporium was a portfolio company of the fintech venture firm Anthemis and was previously listed on the London Stock Exchange. The company is now defunct: it has been delisted, publishes no developer portal or public API, and its primary domain (mporium.com) is parked and listed for sale. This profile is retained as a historical company record in the API Evangelist network; there is no live API surface to enrich.

companies.name: Murmur Technologies INC
companies.description: Murmur Technologies INC (Murmur) is a Chicago, Illinois out-of-home advertising technology company operating a mobile digital billboard platform. It mounts smart LCD screens on car-tops and pedestrian backpacks to display geo-targeted ads on city streets, using sensors, computer vision, and location data to segment audiences by demographics, location, and behavior, measure ad performance in real time, and retarget viewers across other channels such as Facebook and Google. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass its public web hosts (murmurcars.com / murmurads.com) do not resolve to a live web server and the operation appears dormant; it exposes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or documentation.

companies.name: Mybuys
companies.description: MyBuys was a San Mateo, California cross-channel retail personalization company founded in 2002 that delivered coordinated product recommendations and targeted offers across websites, email, and display advertising using a patented portfolio of real-time optimization algorithms and an Active Shopper Database. MyBuys merged with digital advertising firm Magnetic in 2015, and Magnetic sold the MyBuys merchandising/personalization business to Evergage in January 2018. The company is defunct as an independent entity; the mybuys.com domain resolves but serves no live product, and there is no developer portal, documentation, or public API surface to enrich.

companies.name: Neolane
companies.description: Neolane was a marketing automation and cross-channel campaign management company, backed by Battery Ventures, that Adobe acquired in 2013 for roughly $600M and rebranded as Adobe Campaign. The former neolane.com domain now 301-redirects to Adobe's Campaign product page, and the company no longer operates an independent developer portal, API, or artifact surface of its own. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead stub; its live API footprint, if any, belongs to Adobe Campaign rather than a standalone Neolane brand.

companies.name: Node.io
companies.description: Node (Node.io, legally Node Inc.) was an artificial-intelligence startup founded in 2014 by former Google executive Falon Fatemi. Node marketed an "artificial intuition" platform that combined a customer's CRM data with a large external graph of people and companies to score and predict which prospects, partners, employees, or investors a business should engage next. The company raised roughly $16M from investors including 500 Global, Mark Cuban, Avalon Ventures, Canaan Partners, and Bee Partners. On 2020-08-24 Node Inc. was acquired by SugarCRM, which folded the technology into its sales and CX products rather than continuing to sell it as a standalone product. Node.io no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no developer portal, documentation, or public API; the node.io domain is now a parked GoDaddy/Afternic "for sale" listing. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical company record with no live API surface to enrich.

companies.name: Novocall
companies.description: Novocall was a Singapore-based callback and lead-conversion SaaS (a click-to-call and callback-scheduling widget that turned website visitors into inbound phone calls and booked meetings), surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of the July 2026 enrichment pass the company's public web presence is unreachable. The apex novocall.co has live email DNS (SPF, DMARC quarantine, CAA) but no web host, www.novocall.co returns a Cloudflare 530 (origin down), novocall.com is a parked/for-sale domain, and getnovocall.com refuses connections. No public API, developer portal, or documentation surface could be reached, so no API artifacts were harvested; only a live domain-security probe of the remaining DNS/TLS footprint was captured.

companies.name: Offerfit
companies.description: OfferFit is an AI decisioning company whose reinforcement-learning platform automated marketing experimentation and 1:1 personalization (replacing manual A/B testing with self-learning agents). OfferFit was acquired by Braze in 2025 and its product now ships as the BrazeAI Decisioning Studio. The offerfit.ai domain 301-redirects entirely to braze.com, and OfferFit publishes no independent developer API, documentation, SDK, or developer portal of its own. This profile was surfaced as a Menlo Ventures portfolio company and enriched via live DNS/TLS/HTTP domain probes.

companies.name: Omniture
companies.description: Omniture was a web analytics company founded in 1996 in Orem, Utah and backed by Battery Ventures. It went public in 2006 and was acquired by Adobe Systems in 2009 for approximately 1.8 billion dollars. Its flagship SiteCatalyst product became Adobe Analytics within the Adobe Experience Cloud, and the DataWarehouse and reporting interfaces were folded into Adobe's Analytics APIs. The omniture.com domain now redirects to adobe.com and no independent Omniture API surface exists. This profile is retained as an acquired-company lead in the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: OneCommand
companies.description: OneCommand is a cloud-based customer marketing and loyalty-automation platform built for automotive dealerships. Founded in 1999 and headquartered in Mason, Ohio, it helps dealers drive service and sales traffic, increase owner retention, and lower marketing costs through data-driven, multichannel outreach across voice, text, email, and direct mail. Its product family includes the OneCommand loyalty-automation platform, the Higher Gear CRM, and the TrafficAccelerator service. OneCommand was acquired by Affinitiv and its capabilities are now part of Karmotive, a CDK Global company. OneCommand operates as a marketing-services provider and does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or API documentation.

companies.name: OneSpot
companies.description: OneSpot was an Austin, Texas adtech and content-marketing startup that built a machine-learning platform to personalize and sequence branded content across websites, email, and paid media. Founded around 2010 and backed by early investors including 500 Startups, RSL Venture Partners, and Austin angels, it raised multiple venture rounds before being acquired. The onespot.com domain (and its developer, api, and app subdomains) now redirects to IgniteTech, and the company no longer operates an independent public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface.

companies.name: Origami Logic
companies.description: Origami Logic was a marketing-intelligence / big-data analytics company (backed by Accel and Lightspeed Venture Partners) surfaced as a VC-portfolio lead in the API Evangelist network. As of the 2026-07-20 enrichment pass the origamilogic.com web surface is defunct: DNS resolves only Google Workspace mail (MX + SPF/DMARC) with no A record on the apex or www host, so there is no live website, developer portal, documentation, or API surface to enrich. Domain-security posture was probed and recorded; no other public API artifacts exist. Retained as a historical company profile.

companies.name: Outfittery
companies.description: Outfittery is a European personal-shopping and personalized-fashion e-commerce service that curates and ships tailored outfits to customers based on a style questionnaire and human stylist recommendations. Headquartered in Berlin, Germany, it operates across the UK, Spain, France, Germany, Switzerland, Austria, Belgium, the Netherlands and Sweden. Surfaced as a portfolio company of HV Capital and Northzone and added to the API Evangelist network. An enrichment probe found a consumer web/e-commerce presence with no public developer portal, API, or documentation surface.

companies.name: Peerflix Media Network
companies.description: Peerflix Media Network was a Palo Alto, California online movie vertical advertising network that grew out of Peerflix, a peer-to-peer DVD-trading marketplace backed by Battery Ventures, 3i Group, and BV Capital (~$10M raised across two rounds). Peerflix shut down its DVD trading marketplace in April 2008 and continued briefly as the ad-focused Peerflix Media Network before being acquired by LiveUniverse in September 2008. The company is defunct; its domain (peerflixmedianetwork.com) no longer resolves and it exposes no developer platform, documentation, or API surface. Retained in the API Evangelist network as a Battery Ventures portfolio-history record.

companies.name: PICT
companies.description: PICT was a San Francisco startup (founded 2012 by Brent Locks, Kele Dobrinski, and Gregory Nicholas) that built a platform to make images shoppable, letting publishers tag and monetize products within photos. It raised a $1.4M seed round in 2013 backed by 500 Global, Opus Capital, Lowercase Capital, and Forerunner Ventures, and was acquired by PopSugar in January 2014. The pict.com domain no longer resolves and the company exposes no public API surface.

companies.name: Punchd
companies.description: Punchd was a mobile customer-loyalty rewards application for small businesses, founded in 2009 at Cal Poly San Luis Obispo by Reed Morse and Grantland Chew, that let merchants run digital punch-card loyalty programs. Google acquired the company in June 2011 and retired the product in June 2013, folding features into other Google products. The getpunchd.com domain now serves only a static Google-hosted closure announcement. The company is defunct with no active product, developer program, or public API surface; this profile is retained for network completeness as a historical record.

companies.name: Quantum
companies.description: Quantum is a Saudi Arabian advertising-technology (adtech) enabler that bridges online publishers and advertisers with data and technology. Its Quantum One omnichannel platform connects online and offline retail experiences across programmatic ads, in-app media buying, e-sampling, on-ground activations, influencer marketing, and out-of-home media, with goal-attainment tracking, ROI measurement, customer-engagement analytics, and conversion-rate analysis. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal.

companies.name: QuBit
companies.description: QuBit was a London-based ecommerce personalization and product-discovery platform — customer-experience optimization, recommendations, A/B testing, and behavioral big-data analytics — backed by Accel, Balderton Capital, and Sapphire Ventures. QuBit was acquired by Coveo in 2021 and fully absorbed into the Coveo Merchandising Hub. The qubit.com domain, its developer docs (docs.qubit.com), and every API and /.well-known/ endpoint now redirect to coveo.com and docs.coveo.com, so QuBit no longer operates an independent public API surface.

companies.name: Rapportive
companies.description: Rapportive was a browser extension that added a contact-intelligence sidebar to Gmail, surfacing a person's name, photo, job, and social profiles alongside their email. Founded in 2011 and backed by 500 Global (then 500 Startups), it was acquired by LinkedIn in 2012 and later folded into LinkedIn Sales Navigator. The rapportive.com domain now 301-redirects to LinkedIn's "Sales Navigator for Gmail" feature page. Rapportive published no standalone developer API and operates no independent developer surface today; this profile records that defunct/absorbed status for the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: RareLee
companies.description: RareLee (Rarelee) is a Seoul-based premium personal style consulting company founded in 2017, offering data-driven hair, makeup, and fashion analysis. Its consultants classify a client's face shape, features, and skeletal structure across millions of type combinations to recommend personalized hairstyles, makeup designs, and coordinated outfits, both online and in person. Rarelee serves celebrity clientele and has collaborated with brands such as Shinsegae and Marriott. It is a direct-to-consumer service with no public API, developer portal, or technical integration surface; it was added to the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio lead for enrichment.

companies.name: Red Ventures
companies.description: Red Ventures is a privately held digital marketing and media holding company headquartered in Fort Mill, South Carolina, operating a portfolio of high-growth consumer brands and comparison, commerce, and content businesses including Bankrate, The Points Guy, Lonely Planet, and Allconnect. The company combines proprietary technology, data science, and performance marketing to acquire customers on behalf of its brands and partners. It is a corporate/media holding company and publishes no public developer API program, developer portal, or SDKs on its primary web presence.

companies.name: Reply.ai
companies.description: Reply.ai was a conversational AI and customer-experience platform founded in 2016 in New York City, building software to automate repetitive customer-service processes and deliver instant, personalized support across a customer's preferred communication channels. The company was acquired by Kustomer in May 2020 and folded into that platform. As of this enrichment pass the reply.ai domain is a parked "for sale" listing with no active product, developer portal, or public API surface, so no API artifacts could be harvested.

companies.name: Replyr.ai
companies.description: Replyr.ai (Replyr Sdn Bhd, Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia) is an AI-powered customer engagement and lead-acquisition platform. It builds GPT-style chat assistants that reply instantly in multiple languages across WhatsApp and other chat channels to qualify leads, answer FAQs, recommend products, and book appointments 24/7. The company packages this with Meta and Google advertising campaigns and a BookAClinic discovery marketplace, positioning itself as a patient-acquisition solution for specialised clinics. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; as of this enrichment pass Replyr.ai publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable API surface.

companies.name: Rightpoint
companies.description: Rightpoint is a global experience consultancy, now fully integrated into the Genpact brand, that designs and builds customer and employee experiences for enterprise organizations. Its practice spans agentic experience, digital workspace, experience advisory, intelligent content, omnichannel experience, and personalization and experimentation, delivered through deep platform partnerships with Adobe, Microsoft, Optimizely, and Sitecore. As a services and consulting firm rather than an API product company, Rightpoint publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface; this profile captures its identity and web presence within the API Evangelist network. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners.

companies.name: Rocketrip
companies.description: Rocketrip was a New York City corporate travel cost-savings platform that gave business travelers a personalized budget (a "Price to Beat") and rewarded employees who booked flights, hotels, and rail below it, sharing the savings between the traveler and the company. It was backed by Canaan Partners, GV, Bessemer, and Y Combinator. As of this enrichment pass the rocketrip.com and www.rocketrip.com domains 301-redirect to Tabhi (tabhi.ai / tabhi.com), the developer, docs, and api subdomains no longer resolve, and no public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI could be found — the standalone Rocketrip product and its API surface appear to have been retired or folded into Tabhi.

companies.name: ruhnn
companies.description: Ruhnn Holding Limited (如涵控股) is a Hangzhou-based Chinese influencer (KOL) incubation, marketing, and e-commerce company. It pioneered the "internet celebrity" (wanghong) commercialization model, signing and developing influencers and monetizing their audiences through self-operated online stores on marketplaces such as Taobao and Tmall, as well as through a platform/advertising business that connects its network of KOLs with third-party brands for social-marketing campaigns. The company listed on NASDAQ under the ticker RUHN in 2019 and was subsequently taken private. It is surfaced here as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. Ruhnn is a consumer-facing influencer marketing and commerce operator and does not publish a public developer platform, API, or SDK surface.

companies.name: Saleo
companies.description: Saleo is an AI-powered demo experience platform for go-to-market teams, enabling sales and pre-sales engineers to run high-stakes live demos inside their native product, build self-serve interactive product tours, and deliver autonomous AI-driven demos around the clock. Its products include Live (real demos backed by AI-generated demo data), Demo Agent (autonomous AI discovery agents), and Capture (interactive product tours). Saleo serves enterprise customers including SAP, Salesforce, 6sense, Seismic, and SailPoint, and is backed by Emergence Capital. No public developer API surface was found during enrichment; this profile tracks the company for the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Sampler
