companies.description: Sampler is a digital product-sampling platform used by consumer packaged goods (CPG) and retail brands to run targeted sample-distribution campaigns, collect first-party consumer data and reviews, and measure the impact of sampling on purchase behavior. It is operated as a business-facing marketing SaaS (Webflow marketing site, Salesforce Pardot marketing automation) and does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, documentation host, or machine discovery surface at this time.

companies.name: Seam AI
companies.description: Seam AI was an AI-native account-based marketing (ABM) platform that used AI agents to research target accounts, monitor buying signals, and automatically execute outbound marketing and sales campaigns. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, the company has been acquired and is merging its product into Clarify as "Clarify Signals" — a signals-aware CRM. As of this enrichment pass the getseam.ai site serves an acquisition/transition notice directing users to the Clarify Signals waitlist, and the company publishes no public API, developer documentation, SDKs, or .well-known discovery surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead record.

companies.name: ShareRoot
companies.description: ShareRoot is an Australian digital marketing and technology company based in St Kilda, Victoria, that helps brands understand market opportunities and engage audiences across digital channels. It operates through several subsidiary brands: the ShareRoot platform for user-generated content (UGC) and brand ambassador programs (social walls, contests, and e-commerce optimization), The Social Science marketing agency focused on Australia's life sciences and health technology sectors, and Ludomade, which builds digital experiences spanning web design, mobile games, VR/AR, and experiential activations. ShareRoot publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or SDKs; this profile captures the company identity and a live domain-security probe for the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Sigstr
companies.description: Sigstr was an Indianapolis-based email signature marketing and account-based marketing (ABM) platform that turned employee email signatures into a targeted marketing channel, backed by Battery Ventures and other investors. It was acquired by Terminus in September 2019 and folded into the Terminus platform as its Email Experiences / signature marketing product; the standalone Sigstr brand has since been retired. As of this enrichment pass the sigstr.com domain is a parked WP Engine page (HTTP 404), no api./developer. hosts resolve, and app.sigstr.com CNAMEs to Terminus infrastructure (email2.terminusplatform.com) — the company publishes no public API surface to enrich.

companies.name: Silveredge
companies.description: Silveredge was added to the API Evangelist network as a stub from the 500 Global venture portfolio; the website property wired to this record (silverpush.co) presents Silverpush, an AI-powered contextual intelligence company that helps advertisers deliver contextually relevant, brand-safe video advertising across YouTube, CTV, TikTok, Meta, and the open web through its Mirrors contextual intelligence suite and Parallels moment-marketing platform. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or /.well-known discovery surface — developer subdomains do not resolve and developer paths return 404 — so there is no API artifact surface to harvest. This profile remains a company lead.

companies.name: Simply Measured
companies.description: Simply Measured was a Seattle-based social media analytics and reporting platform, founded in 2010 and backed by Trinity Ventures, that measured brand performance across Twitter, Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, LinkedIn and other social channels. It was acquired by Sprout Social in December 2017 and its product, brand, and developer surface were sunset and folded into Sprout Social. The simplymeasured.com domain now 301-redirects to sproutsocial.com and no independent Simply Measured API, developer portal, or documentation remains online. This record is retained as a defunct/acquired portfolio-lead marker; there is no live API surface to enrich.

companies.name: Smart Reno
companies.description: Smart Reno is a Montreal-based home-renovation marketplace, founded in 2012 by Andrei Uglar, that connects homeowners with qualified, available local contractors. Homeowners post a project and receive up to three competing quotes from vetted renovation professionals through a proprietary contractor-matching platform. Backed by 500 Startups (500 Global), Anges Quebec, and BDC, Smart Reno was acquired by RBC Ventures in 2019 and now operates its consumer marketplace under the soumissionrenovation.ca brand across Quebec, Ontario, and Alberta. The company exposes no public developer API, SDK, documentation portal, or webhook surface; smartreno.com 301-redirects to the successor site and no /.well-known discovery documents were found.

companies.name: StrikeAd
companies.description: StrikeAd was a mobile advertising technology company surfaced as a portfolio company of Uncork Capital and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead. As of this enrichment pass its primary domain (strikead.com) resolves to a parked lander page rather than an active product or developer surface - every path, including the homepage, /.well-known/ discovery endpoints, and common API paths, returns the same domain-parking redirect to /lander. No developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI definition, or other machine-readable API surface could be found, indicating the company is no longer operating an active public API.

companies.name: SumAll
companies.description: SumAll was a New York-based social media and business analytics startup, surfaced as a portfolio company of battery-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the company is defunct - its primary domain sumall.com no longer resolves to a live product and is parked/listed for sale on Afternic. There is no live developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI, SDK, or documentation surface to harvest, so no provider artifacts were produced.

companies.name: Super
companies.description: Super (super.gs) is an early-stage consumer entertainment application built by Outpace Studios and backed by Bullpen Capital, positioned around the tagline "Entertainment you can cash out." As of mid-2026 the product is pre-launch: the public site is a single-page marketing and waitlist experience with no published developer platform, API, SDKs, or documentation. This API Evangelist profile tracks Super as a portfolio lead and currently carries only a live domain-security probe of super.gs; it will be enriched further if and when the company ships a public API surface.

companies.name: Survata
companies.description: Survata was a San Francisco market-research and brand-measurement company, backed by Bloomberg Beta, that ran online surveys and brand-lift studies to measure advertising effectiveness across digital channels. Survata was acquired by Upwave in 2019 and the brand has since been fully absorbed — survata.com now 301-redirects to upwave.com, the enterprise brand-measurement platform. No public developer API, documentation, developer portal, or well-known discovery surface is published for Survata or its Upwave successor; this profile is retained as a network lead with no live API surface.

companies.name: Sweetgreen
companies.description: Sweetgreen is a fast-casual restaurant company (NYSE: SG) building healthy, plant-forward food through a network of company-owned locations and its digital ordering platform. It reaches customers primarily via its consumer website and mobile app for pickup, delivery, and its Sweetgreen Rewards loyalty program, and operates automated "Infinite Kitchen" locations. As of this enrichment pass, Sweetgreen publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API specifications; this profile captures its public web presence and probed domain-security posture only. Backed by D1 Capital and True Ventures.

companies.name: TapCommerce (Twitter)
companies.description: TapCommerce was a mobile app-retargeting and advertising technology company acquired by Twitter in July 2014 and folded into Twitter's MoPub mobile ad exchange; it no longer operates as an independent entity. Surfaced as a portfolio company of bain-capital-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. Sector: commerce / adtech. Enrichment pass (2026-07-21) found no live domain (tapcommerce.com does not resolve) and no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or documentation surface to enrich.

companies.name: Tapsense
companies.description: TapSense was a mobile advertising and real-time-bidding platform surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. The 2026-07-21 enrichment pass found no live developer or API surface - the tapsense.com domain resolves to a parked page with no content, the docs.tapsense.com host presents an expired TLS certificate, and developer.tapsense.com returns no documentation. No OpenAPI, SDK, package, MCP, or webhook surface was discoverable. The company appears defunct (mobile-ad platforms of this era were commonly acquired and wound down), so there is nothing to enrich beyond this identity record.

companies.name: Telaria
companies.description: Telaria was an independent supply-side platform (SSP) for premium video and connected TV (CTV) advertising, formerly known as Tremor Video's sell-side business. Its Video Management Platform (VMP) combined an ad server built for advanced/OTT TV with real-time analytics, automated decisioning, yield optimization, and integrated programmatic plus direct-sold monetization for publishers of digital video inventory. On April 1, 2020 Telaria completed an all-stock merger of equals with Rubicon Project to form Magnite, now the largest independent sell-side advertising platform spanning CTV, desktop, and mobile. Telaria no longer operates as a standalone company: the telaria.com domain redirects to magnite.com, and the "Telaria" name survives publicly only as a Prebid.js header-bidding bidder adapter routed through Magnite. This profile documents the historical company; there is no independent public developer API, OpenAPI definition, SDK, or documentation portal to harvest.

companies.name: TellApart
companies.description: TellApart was a predictive-marketing and cross-device retargeting technology company founded in 2009 by former Google AdWords-API engineers Josh McFarland and Mark Ayzenshtat. Its cloud-based customer data platform unified shopper profiles across channels and devices and used machine-learning scoring to power dynamic product ads and direct-response retargeting for retailers such as Neiman Marcus, Wayfair, Sur La Table and Pottery Barn. TellApart was acquired by Twitter in April 2015 for roughly $533M in stock and folded into Twitter's advertising business; it no longer operates as an independent company and the tellapart.com domain is now parked with no live developer or API surface. Surfaced as a Greylock portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment.

companies.name: TellApart (acquired by Twitter in 2015)
companies.description: TellApart (acquired by Twitter in 2015) is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of bain-capital-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: ai-apps. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

companies.name: thetab
companies.description: The Tab (thetab.com) is a UK-based digital media and entertainment publication operated by Digitalbox Publishing Ltd (Co Reg No. 09909897). It covers celebrity and reality-TV news, viral trends, gaming, politics, and university and campus culture across a network of youth-focused verticals, monetized primarily through advertising (advertise.thetab.com). Surfaced as a portfolio company of balderton-capital and added to the API Evangelist network. As of the 2026-07-21 enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI, /.well-known/ discovery surface, or llms.txt (all probed and returned HTTP 404); this remains an editorial/advertising media property with no developer-facing product.

companies.name: Tout
companies.description: Tout (ToutApp) was a sales engagement platform offering email tracking, templates, and analytics for sales teams, and a 500 Global portfolio company. ToutApp was acquired by Marketo in 2017 and became Marketo Sales Connect; toutapp.com now 301-redirects to the Marketo Sales Connect product page on business.adobe.com following Adobe's acquisition of Marketo. Tout no longer operates a standalone developer or API surface.

companies.name: ToutApp
companies.description: ToutApp was a sales-engagement platform founded in 2011 by Tawheed Kader that gave sales teams email templates, email tracking, campaigns, and analytics for outbound selling, backed by Andreessen Horowitz. Marketo acquired ToutApp in May 2017 and folded the product into Marketo Sales Connect (later part of Adobe after Adobe acquired Marketo in 2018). The company is defunct as a standalone business - toutapp.com now redirects to Adobe's Marketo Sales Connect page - and no independent ToutApp API or developer surface remains publicly available.

companies.name: Tracksby
companies.description: Tracksby (Tracks.by) was a music marketing startup that helped artists and their managers release new music and videos through deep Facebook integration, social launch campaigns, fan email capture, and YouTube/VEVO embeds, turning each release into a fan-growth campaign. Listed on the a16z investment list, the early-2010s company is now defunct - tracks.by no longer resolves, tracksby.com is parked for sale, the @TracksBy Twitter account is gone, and its GitHub account has been inactive since 2012. No public API surface was found, so this profile records an inactive portfolio lead with no artifacts to enrich.

companies.name: Tripplus
companies.description: TripPlus (點數旅遊) is a Taiwan-based travel-rewards and loyalty-points platform. It provides airline mileage award-ticket search and redemption tools, curated recommendations and comparisons of US travel credit cards, and a marketplace for buying and selling airline miles and reward points. The consumer-facing site (tripplus.cc) is fronted by Cloudflare and, as of this enrichment pass, exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or documented well-known endpoints. Backed by 500 Global; tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead.

companies.name: TrueLens
companies.description: TrueLens was a marketing-technology startup providing social media analytics and customer intelligence. Its product, Socialgraphics, helped brands target customers using data compiled and analyzed from multiple social networks for marketing campaigns. Google Ventures (GV) led a roughly $1.2M funding round in 2012; the company was small (2-10 employees). TrueLens now appears defunct: its former domain truelens.com 301-redirects to an unrelated retailer (misterspex.de), and no public API, developer portal, or documentation could be found. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a GV portfolio lead; there is no live API surface to enrich.

companies.name: Trust
companies.description: Trust (Trust Software Inc., trust.co) was a fintech and marketing-technology startup founded in 2019 by James Borow, backed by a 2020 seed investment from Lightspeed Venture Partners. It began as a corporate card and community giving digital businesses higher credit limits and extended payment terms on marketing spend, then pivoted to Market (withmarket.com), an AI marketing assistant that let Shopify merchants chat with their business data. As of July 2026 both trust.co and withmarket.com no longer resolve in DNS and the company appears to have wound down. No public API, developer portal, or SDK surface was ever published.

companies.name: TVTY
companies.description: TVTY is an advertising technology company that bridges television and digital advertising through its Moment Marketing platform. Its TV Ad Alert technology detects when a brand or competitor TV spot airs and synchronizes digital media campaigns — search, social, display and marketplace advertising — to those moments so advertisers reach audiences at the point of highest attention. TVTY was a Partech portfolio company serving global brands and media agencies.

companies.name: TXN
companies.description: TXN (TXN Solutions, Inc.) was a San Francisco consumer spending analytics company that captured transactions directly from the credit and debit cards of an opt-in research panel, layering demographics and targeted surveys on top to give merchants competitive intelligence and share-of-wallet insight. Founded by Alex Rampell, Pasha Bitz, and Jonathan Wolf and backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Bloomberg Beta, General Catalyst, Homebrew, SV Angel, and Slow Ventures, it is listed as exited in the Bloomberg Beta portfolio. As of July 2026 txn.com serves only a parked "Launching Soon" page on an Alibaba Cloud host with a self-signed TLS certificate — no product, developer, or API surface remains.

companies.name: Unamo
companies.description: Unamo was a Warsaw, Poland based SaaS suite offering SEO monitoring, social media monitoring, and conversion rate optimization, formerly known as Positionly, and backed by Point Nine Capital. The company appears defunct as of July 2026, with unamo.com no longer resolving in DNS and the pre-rebrand positionly.com site serving stale 2017-era content whose API, signup, terms, and privacy pages return 404. No public API surface, client packages, or developer documentation remain online.

companies.name: URX *
companies.description: URX was a San Francisco mobile deep-linking and app-search startup that connected mobile users to relevant in-app commerce experiences. Backed by roughly $15M from investors including GV (Google Ventures) and CyberAgent, it was acquired by Pinterest in May 2016 and its product was wound down. The urx.com domain is now parked and listed for sale on a domain marketplace, and no API, developer portal, or public developer artifacts remain. Profiled in the API Evangelist network as a historical GV portfolio company.

companies.name: Usermind
companies.description: Usermind was a Seattle-based journey and experience orchestration platform that captured and analyzed contextual data at every touchpoint of the customer journey to personalize experiences across channels, and was named a Leader in The Forrester Wave Journey Orchestration Platforms, Q2 2020. Backed by a16z and Menlo Ventures, the company was acquired by Qualtrics (announced July 20, 2021); usermind.com now redirects to qualtrics.com and no independent Usermind API surface remains.

companies.name: VICI Sports
companies.description: VICI Sports operates FanFest, a white-labeled fan engagement platform for the sports industry that "turns fan engagement into revenue" by recognizing every fan action across stadiums, homes, and bars and rewarding it automatically. The company reports 150+ activations with sports brands and 30M+ fans commercialized, with partners including AC Milan, the Premier League, Paris Saint-Germain, and Manchester City. Backed by Techstars. No public developer/API surface is currently published; the fanfest.vip site is a single-page marketing app with a contact form only.

companies.name: wantful
companies.description: Wantful was a personalized online gift-giving service founded in 2011 by John Poisson, based in San Francisco and New York City, that let shoppers assemble curated gift books of design-forward products which recipients could browse and redeem for the item they most wanted. Backed by Slow Ventures and others (roughly $5.5M raised) and partnered with Nordstrom, the company shut down in September 2013 after failing to secure follow-on funding. It is defunct — wantful.com resolves (Route53 NS) but serves no live product, and there is no API, documentation, or developer surface to enrich.

companies.name: Webhelp
companies.description: Webhelp is a French customer-experience and business-process-outsourcing (BPO) company founded in 2000 and headquartered in Paris, providing outsourced customer support, sales, back-office, content moderation, and payment/collections services to global brands across many languages and geographies. In 2023 Webhelp merged with Concentrix; the combined company operates under the Concentrix brand and the standalone webhelp.com domain no longer resolves to a live website. Webhelp was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Insight Partners. It is a services/BPO operator rather than an API producer and publishes no public developer portal, OpenAPI definition, or client SDKs; the enrichment pipeline found no public API surface to catalog.

companies.name: Wildfire Interactive
companies.description: Wildfire Interactive, Inc. was a social media marketing software company founded in 2008 by Victoria Ransom and Alain Chuard in Redwood City, California. Its platform let brands create, optimize, and measure their presence across social networks — running branded promotions, sweepstakes, contests, and coupons plus page management, advertising, messaging, and analytics across Facebook, Twitter, Pinterest, and YouTube. Backed by the Facebook Fund, Summit Partners, Accel Partners, and Founders Fund, Wildfire was acquired by Google in 2012 and folded into Google's advertising products (DoubleClick); the standalone product was wound down by 2014. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of uncork-capital and is retained as a historical record — the company operates no independent public API surface today.

companies.name: Wonderbly *
companies.description: Wonderbly is an online publisher that makes personalized books and gifts for kids and adults. Founded in 2013 (originally as Lost My Name), it lets customers design and buy books customized with a recipient's name, themes, and occasion, and has delighted over 10 million readers worldwide. The consumer e-commerce site operates across 40+ language and regional storefronts (US, UK, AU, CA, DE, FR, NL, IT, ES). Backed by GV. No public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation was found during enrichment; this remains a company profile lead in the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: xchange (Formerly Exchange Applications Inc.)
companies.description: Xchange Inc., formerly Exchange Applications Inc., was a Boston-based (89 South Street, Boston, MA) customer relationship marketing software company that helped enterprises earn a greater share of their customers' business through relevant, personalized customer communications, selling campaign-management and customer-analytics software. A Delaware corporation backed by Insight Partners, it went public in 1998 (S-1 filed 1998-07-22, SEC CIK 0001065857, SIC 7373 Computer Integrated Systems Design). The company went dark after its final 10-Q on 2002-11-19, and the SEC revoked its Exchange Act registration on 2011-01-07. Both historical domains are now parked: xchange.com carries no A record and exchangeapplications.com is a domain-for-sale lander. The company is defunct with no website, developer surface, or APIs; this profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead record.

companies.name: YesPath
companies.description: YesPath was an account engagement platform based in San Francisco that helped B2B sales and marketing teams reach and win large target accounts, using machine learning to surface real-time recommendations on the right content and next best action for each account. The company was acquired by Medium in April 2017 and no longer operates as an independent product; the yespath.com domain still resolves to AWS IP addresses but serves no live web application. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. Enrichment found no live developer, API, or documentation surface to harvest — the entry is retained for portfolio-graph completeness.

companies.name: Yodle
companies.description: Yodle was a New York-based local online marketing and lead-generation company for small and medium-sized businesses, offering all-in-one advertising, web presence, and business-automation products such as Marketing Essentials, Yodle Ads, and Lighthouse 360. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, it was acquired by Web.com in February 2016 for roughly $342 million and no longer operates as a standalone brand — its technology was folded into Web.com, now part of Newfold Digital. Yodle exposes no public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs; api.yodle.com is an internal, auth-gated endpoint (HTTP 401) and the legacy www.yodle.com site is effectively defunct.

companies.name: Alphabet
companies.description: The parent company of Google and one of the world's most valuable corporations. Operates the dominant search engine, Android mobile OS, YouTube, Google Cloud, and Waymo autonomous vehicles alongside numerous technology ventures.

companies.name: Hatch Loyalty
companies.description: Hatch Loyalty (formerly Belly) was a Chicago-based customer activation, loyalty, and engagement platform for enterprise retailers, with a strong focus on the fuel and convenience-store vertical. It aggregated customer data across a retailer's business systems to build customer profiles and ran a rules engine over submitted transactions to trigger offers and redemptions. Hatch exposed a RESTful developer platform (the "Hatch HUB" API) that conformed to the JSON:API specification, with a public developer portal, API reference, and transaction-processing tutorials. The company was backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Lightbank, NEA, and DAG Ventures, and was acquired by Stuzo around 2019-2020 (the earlier Belly product line was sold to Mobivity). As of this profile the hatchloyalty.com domain and all of its subdomains (www, developer, api) are parked and listed for sale, so no live API or developer surface remains to enrich.

companies.name: GTM Release
companies.description: A network index of companies, organizations, and platforms relevant to the Naftiko Framework go-to-market release strategy, covering press, developer communities, directories, review platforms, podcasts, business directories, and events.

companies.name: Stagwell
companies.description: Stagwell is a digital-first global marketing services and technology company and a Fortune 1000 firm. The company operates a network of agencies and technology brands and offers the Stagwell Marketing Cloud (SMC), a suite of proprietary marketing technology products built by its in-house engineering teams. Stagwell does not publish a single unified public developer portal at the holding-company level; product APIs are exposed through individual SMC products.

companies.name: CardSpring
companies.description: CardSpring was a card-linked offers and payments platform that provided an API for building card-linked applications, letting developers connect merchant point-of-sale systems and consumer payment cards to deliver digital coupons, loyalty rewards, and receipt-level offers. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and DCVC and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. The company was acquired by Twitter in 2014 and subsequently wound down; as of this pass every path on cardspring.com (including the old /help/developer_faq.html) 307-redirects to an Afternic "cardspring.com is for sale" domain-sale lander, developer.cardspring.com fails TLS with no matching certificate, and no first-party CardSpring packages remain on npm or RubyGems. There is no live developer portal, documentation, API, or OpenAPI surface to enrich. Sector: payments.

companies.name: Paydiant
companies.description: Paydiant was a Boston-based mobile-wallet, point-of-sale and cloud payments platform, backed by General Catalyst, that let banks, merchants and retailers build their own white-label mobile-payment and loyalty apps (notably powering the retailer-led MCX "CurrentC" wallet). PayPal acquired Paydiant in 2015 and folded the technology into its in-store and merchant products; Paydiant no longer operates as an independent company. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a General Catalyst portfolio lead; an enrichment probe on 2026-07-20 found no live independent API surface — the paydiant.com domain and its api/developer/docs subdomains wildcard-resolve to a PayPal/MarkMonitor brand-protection parking IP (3.33.139.32) and serve no content.

companies.name: MaxPoint
companies.description: MaxPoint is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of trinity-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: marketing. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

companies.name: Mosaic
companies.description: Mosaic is a brand experience agency offering experiential marketing, B2B corporate experiences, integrated commerce, and field sales and marketing services. The agency builds brand-building, conversion-driving experiences for clients across multiple channels.

companies.name: Omnicom Group
companies.description: Omnicom Group is a global advertising, marketing, and corporate communications holding company with hundreds of agencies serving clients in more than 100 countries. The Omni platform is positioned as an AI-driven marketing intelligence platform but no public APIs are documented at this time.

companies.name: PerfectMarket
companies.description: PerfectMarket is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of trinity-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: marketing. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

companies.name: TubeMogul
companies.description: TubeMogul is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of trinity-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: marketing. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

companies.name: Quad/Graphics
companies.description: Quad/Graphics is a worldwide marketing solutions company that provides print and integrated marketing services helping marketers reach today's consumers across multiple channels.

bands.label: Not Yet Rated
bands.blurb: Providers we have not scored yet — unknown, not zero.

companies.name: 500 Global
companies.description: 500 Global (formerly 500 Startups) is a global venture capital firm and startup accelerator founded in 2010 by Dave McClure and Christine Tsai and headquartered in Palo Alto / Silicon Valley, California. The firm invests from pre-seed to pre-IPO in globally ambitious technology founders, built on the belief that "talent lives everywhere, but capital and opportunity does not." 500 Global pioneered a "lots of little bets" seed strategy, backing hundreds of companies per fund with smaller initial checks, and has grown one of the industry's largest truly global seed portfolios: 3,000+ companies across 80+ countries with $300B+ in cumulative portfolio valuation, including 35+ companies valued at $1B+ and 160+ valued at more than $100M. It runs regional and thematic practices spanning Southeast Asia, Latin America, MENA, Africa, Japan, Korea, Thailand, and Eurasia, plus a Sustainable Growth strategy (health, climate, agriculture, gender, education), flagship accelerator programs, and the VC Unlocked investor-education program that has trained 1,400+ investors. As of April 30, 2025 the firm reported approximately $2.3B in assets under management. Notable investments include Canva, Grab, Talkdesk, Credit Karma, Twilio, and Bukalapak.

companies.name: AUTHORS.md
companies.description: AUTHORS.md is a file format standard used in open-source and collaborative software projects to list the original creators, primary authors, and significant contributors of a project. Often required by open-source licenses such as GPL and Apache 2.0 to provide proper attribution, the AUTHORS.md file documents who wrote what portions of a codebase, their email addresses, and the scope of their contributions. Related standards include CONTRIBUTORS.md, All Contributors specification, and REUSE/SPDX contributor attribution frameworks.

companies.name: Balderton Capital
companies.description: Balderton Capital is a London-headquartered venture capital firm focused exclusively on backing European-founded technology companies. Founded in 2000 as Benchmark Capital Europe and fully independent since 2007, Balderton is one of Europe's largest and most established venture firms, with over $7 billion in assets under management across dedicated early-stage and growth funds. The firm invests from Seed through Series B and follows on into growth stages, writing checks across sectors including fintech, artificial intelligence, B2B SaaS, developer tools and infrastructure, digital health, gaming, marketplaces and climate. Balderton is known for a founder-centric model, running a dedicated founder wellbeing and performance platform and an executive/talent network to support portfolio companies. Notable investments over the firm's history include Revolut, GoCardless, Depop, Darktrace, Contentful, Dream Games, Wayve, Aircall, Citymapper, Talend, MySQL, Recorded Future, Sophia Genetics and The Hut Group (THG).

companies.name: CONTRIBUTORS.md
companies.description: CONTRIBUTORS.md is an open source convention used to recognize the people and organizations that have contributed to a project. The file lists contributors by name, GitHub handle, and contribution type, ranging from code and documentation to design, testing, accessibility, and community organization. CONTRIBUTORS.md is often paired with the All Contributors specification, which standardizes contribution categories using emoji keys and supports automated table generation through the All Contributors bot.

companies.name: Electric Capital
companies.description: Electric Capital is an engineering-led venture capital firm founded in 2018 and headquartered in Palo Alto, California, investing in founders building frontier technologies across crypto, cryptography, distributed systems, and AI. The firm backs user-owned technology and cryptographic infrastructure that reduces reliance on intermediaries and gives users control, privacy, and access. Electric Capital invests from pre-seed through growth, with typical checks ranging from roughly $1M to $15M+, and has deployed more than $3B since inception across multiple funds (including a $1B raise announced in 2022). Its portfolio spans DeFi, layer-1 and layer-2 infrastructure, exchanges, developer tools, security, identity, and select AI, fintech, healthcare, and deep-tech companies, with notable investments including Solana, Kraken, EigenLayer/EigenCloud, dYdX, Magic Eden, Sui/Mysten Labs, NEAR, Consensys, and Aave. The firm is also known for authoring the widely cited annual Electric Capital Developer Report.

companies.name: Founders Fund
companies.description: Founders Fund is a San Francisco-based venture capital firm founded in 2005 by Peter Thiel, Ken Howery, and Luke Nosek, best known for the credo "we wanted flying cars, instead we got 140 characters" and a contrarian appetite for hard science and frontier technology over incremental consumer apps. The firm backs category-defining, often monopoly-scale companies across aerospace and defense, artificial intelligence, biotech, fintech and crypto, energy, semiconductors, robotics, and deep tech, investing from seed through late-stage growth with an increasingly concentrated, high-conviction style (its recent growth funds put hundreds of millions of dollars into a small number of companies). Founders Fund manages roughly $17 billion in assets as of 2025 and is headquartered at the Letterman Digital Arts Center in San Francisco's Presidio. Its portfolio includes many of the defining technology companies of the era, among them SpaceX, Palantir, Anduril, Stripe, Airbnb, Facebook, Neuralink, OpenAI, DeepMind, Ramp, Nubank, Spotify, and Figma.

companies.name: General Catalyst
companies.description: General Catalyst is a global venture capital and investment firm founded in 2000 by Joel Cutler and David Fialkow, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, with offices in San Francisco, New York, London, Berlin, Bengaluru, and Washington, D.C. The firm invests across seed, venture, and growth stages and manages more than $43 billion in assets under management (as of December 2024), backing 900+ portfolio companies. General Catalyst operates through distinct capital vehicles and initiatives — Ignition/Seed for early-stage, Endurance/Grow for growth, Creation for company building, and a dedicated Health Assurance practice for healthcare transformation. Its current "Global Resilience" thesis, led by CEO Hemant Taneja, concentrates on the critical systems that underpin modern society — healthcare, energy, defense, and AI — alongside an "unscaling" thesis that uses data and AI to personalize core societal services. Notable investments include Airbnb, Stripe, Anthropic, Canva, HubSpot, Ramp, Anduril, Applied Intuition, Samsara, Mistral, Helsing, Hippocratic AI, and Mercor.

companies.name: Hillhouse Investment
companies.description: Hillhouse Investment (formerly Hillhouse Capital) is a global investment firm founded in 2005 by Lei Zhang with seed capital from the Yale University endowment, and is one of Asia's largest private-market investors, managing an estimated US$100 billion in assets as of 2026. Headquartered in Singapore with offices in Hong Kong, Beijing, Shanghai, New York, London, and Abu Dhabi, the firm invests globally across all stages of a company's life cycle, spanning public equities, growth equity, private equity buyouts, venture capital (through its early-stage arm GL Ventures, launched in 2020), and real assets. Hillhouse describes itself as disciplined and pragmatic investors who prioritize business fundamentals and deep, bottom-up industry research, with sector focus on healthcare, industrials, energy transition, business services, and consumer. Its portfolio spans companies headquartered in more than 25 countries and has included category-defining businesses such as Tencent, JD.com, Baidu, Zoom, BeiGene, Miniso, Airbnb, Uber, and Didi. Backers have historically included major university endowments (Yale, Stanford, Princeton, MIT, University of Pennsylvania, University of Texas) and CPPIB.

companies.name: HongShan (HSG)
companies.description: HongShan (HSG), formerly known as Sequoia Capital China, is a leading global venture capital and private equity firm investing across technology, healthcare, and consumer sectors. Founded in 2005 by Neil Shen with early guidance from Sequoia Capital, the firm spun off as an independent entity in 2023-2024, rebranding from Sequoia China to HongShan (a pinyin romanization of its Chinese name, meaning "redwood") while retaining its original Chinese name. HSG invests across the full lifecycle - seed, venture, growth, buyout, and infrastructure - and also runs a public equities business (HCEP). The firm manages over USD 61 billion in assets (as of April 30, 2026) and has backed more than 1,700 companies since inception, with 180+ having gone public and 140+ reaching unicorn status. HSG operates from Hong Kong, Shanghai, Beijing, Shenzhen, London, Tokyo, and Singapore. Notable portfolio companies include Alibaba, ByteDance, Meituan, Pinduoduo, BYD, Nio, Xpeng, Airwallex, Canva, Monzo, and Moderna.

companies.name: ICONIQ Capital
companies.description: ICONIQ Capital is a global investment firm founded in December 2011 by Divesh Makan, Michael Anders, and Chad Boeding, headquartered in San Francisco, California with offices in Palo Alto, New York, London, and Singapore. ICONIQ operates as a hybrid family office and multi-strategy investment firm serving ultra-high-net-worth technology entrepreneurs, executives, and their families, and reports over $100B in assets under management across investment management, real assets, venture and growth, and impact strategies. Its venture arm, ICONIQ Growth, partners with founders from inception through IPO and beyond, backing category-leading technology companies across enterprise software, infrastructure, data, developer tools, fintech, security, healthcare IT, and — since 2023 — artificial intelligence as a core theme. ICONIQ Growth has invested in 140+ companies and produced notable outcomes including Snowflake, Airbnb, GitLab, HashiCorp, Datadog, Docusign, Adyen, Uber, Zoom, and Procore, alongside active AI positions in Anthropic, OpenAI, Writer, Glean, ElevenLabs, and Sierra.

companies.name: Index Ventures
companies.description: Index Ventures is a global venture capital firm founded in Geneva in 1996 by Neil Rimer, David Rimer and Giuseppe Zocco, and headquartered in London with offices in San Francisco, New York, Geneva and Jersey. The firm invests across the full startup lifecycle through dedicated vehicles: Origin (seed), Venture (early-stage) and Growth funds, backing companies from seed to IPO. It focuses on artificial intelligence and machine learning, business applications, data, fintech, security, healthcare, entertainment, media, mobility, retail, open source and the future of work. Index has raised roughly $15B in total capital, including $2.3B announced in 2024 ($800M early-stage, $1.5B later-stage). Notable investments include Adyen, Figma, Datadog, Discord, Revolut, Wise, Robinhood, Roblox, Confluent, Anthropic, Scale AI and Wiz. Its philosophy emphasizes backing founders on character and vision — 'we invest in who you are, not just what you do.'

companies.name: Insight Partners
companies.description: Insight Partners is a global software-focused venture capital and private equity firm founded in 1995 by Jeff Horing and Jerry Murdock and headquartered in New York City, with additional offices in London, Tel Aviv, and Palo Alto. The firm invests in high-growth technology and software ScaleUp companies at every stage from early (Series A) through growth and late-stage pre-IPO, deploying checks that range from roughly $5M up to $500M+ and pairing capital with a dedicated in-house operations team (Insight Onsite) that provides talent, sales, marketing, and product expertise to accelerate scaling. Sector emphasis spans enterprise software broadly, including cybersecurity, fintech, AI/ML, DevOps, data infrastructure, and healthtech. With approximately $90B in regulatory assets under management as of 2025 and more than 875 companies backed worldwide, Insight is one of the largest technology investors in the world, with a portfolio and exit history that includes Twitter, Shopify, DocuSign, Wix, SentinelOne, HelloFresh, N26, Alteryx, and AppDynamics.

companies.name: Lightspeed Venture Partners
companies.description: Lightspeed Venture Partners is a global, multi-stage venture capital firm founded in 2000 by Barry Eggers, Christopher Schaepe, Ravi Mhatre, and Peter Nieh, and headquartered in Menlo Park, California. Lightspeed invests from seed through Series F and beyond, backing bold builders across artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, cloud and enterprise infrastructure, developer tools, fintech, consumer, gaming, and healthcare/biotech. The firm operates as a single global team across roughly a dozen offices in the United States, Europe, Israel, India, and Southeast Asia, with U.S./Europe/Israel run by Lightspeed Management Company (LSVP) and India/Southeast Asia by Lightspeed India Partners (LSIP). Lightspeed reports managing on the order of $25B+ (up to $40B+ by some self-reported figures) across the Lightspeed platform. Notable investments and exits include Anthropic, Mistral AI, ElevenLabs, Wiz, Rubrik, Cato Networks, Stripe, Affirm, Snap, Nutanix, MuleSoft, AppDynamics, Nest, Grafana, ngrok, Faire, and Navan.

companies.name: New Enterprise Associates
companies.description: New Enterprise Associates (NEA) is one of the world's largest and longest-running venture capital firms, founded in 1977 by Dick Kramlich, Chuck Newhall, and Frank Bonsal. Headquartered in Menlo Park, California, with offices in Timonium (Maryland), New York, and London, NEA invests across the full company lifecycle — "from idea to IPO" — spanning seed, Series A, and later growth rounds. The firm has raised over $27 billion in committed capital (as of December 31, 2024) and organizes into specialized practice groups across two core sectors: technology (enterprise software, consumer, fintech, AI, infrastructure) and healthcare (biopharma, life sciences, digital health, and medical devices). NEA is known for an active, hands-on partnership model and long-term support of category-defining companies, with a portfolio that has produced many notable IPOs and acquisitions including Cloudflare, MongoDB, Robinhood, Coursera, Databricks, Plaid, and Tempus.

companies.name: Prosus Ventures
companies.description: Prosus Ventures is the venture-capital arm of Prosus, the Amsterdam-headquartered global consumer-internet and technology group (part of the Naspers group), founded in 2015 to make early-stage and growth-stage technology investments in high-growth markets outside the United States and China. The firm invests to "fuel the ecommerce flywheel," backing companies across food delivery, fintech, consumer services, logistics, e-commerce and marketplaces, plus a strong and growing focus on early-stage AI startups that reshape the e-commerce value chain (shopping and advertising tech, customer support, AI agents and operations) and frontier technologies such as quantum computing, robotics, space and biotech. Prosus Ventures typically invests from seed through Series B and into growth rounds, with a primary geographic focus on India, Latin America and Europe, plus activity in Southeast Asia, the Middle East and ANZ. In fiscal year 2025 the group committed and invested over $400 million across 40+ closed transactions, including roughly $88 million into AI. Its public portfolio spans 80+ companies including Meesho, Urban Company, PharmEasy, Klar, ElasticRun, BandLab, Ema, Corti and Oxford Ionics. The venture team is led by CEO Martin Tschopp with regional heads across India, Europe, Southeast Asia and the Middle East.

companies.name: SV Angel
companies.description: SV Angel is a San Francisco-based venture capital firm founded in 2009 by Ron Conway, one of Silicon Valley's most prolific angel investors. The firm runs two vehicles: an early-stage Seed Fund that writes roughly $200k checks into pre-seed and seed rounds, and a later-stage Growth Fund that invests at Series B and beyond. SV Angel is a founder-first, high-conviction investor that deliberately does not lead rounds, takes no board seats, and writes smaller checks as part of a larger syndicate so it can act as a neutral "routing layer" and advocate for founders. It is famous for its "Inflection Point Approach" — showing up at critical moments around fundraising, M&A, and business development. The firm invests almost entirely in US-based, software-driven companies across consumer and enterprise, and its portfolio has produced dozens of unicorns and landmark outcomes including Google, Airbnb, Coinbase, Stripe, Slack, Instacart, DoorDash, Reddit, Pinterest, GitHub, Databricks, Anthropic, and OpenAI.

companies.name: Tiger Global Management
companies.description: Tiger Global Management is an American investment firm founded in 2001 by Chase Coleman III, headquartered at 9 West 57th Street in New York City. It operates as a "crossover" platform that invests across both public and private markets, running a research-driven, long-term strategy to partner with high-quality, innovative technology companies across every stage of their lifecycle. Tiger Global concentrates on the global internet, software, consumer internet, and financial technology sectors, and its private/venture arm became one of the most prolific startup backers of the 2020-2022 boom, investing in 361 deals in 2021 alone and backing hundreds of growth-stage companies worldwide. Check sizes range from early-stage venture through very large growth and pre-IPO rounds, and the same team follows companies from private markets into the public markets and beyond. The firm reported roughly $55.9B in assets under management as of May 2024, and its portfolio spans North America, Europe, Latin America, India, and China. Notable investments include Stripe, ByteDance, Databricks, Coinbase, Nubank, Snowflake, UiPath, GitLab, and Flipkart.
